Bitcoin rebounds toward $57,500 after a massive $2.55 billion crypto liquidation wave.

A break below the $54,522 support could put Bitcoin’s $49,011 August 2024 low at risk.

Bitcoin open interest fell to $19.73 billion as leveraged positions were rapidly cleared.

In a recent development, bitcoin has bounced back toward $57,500 after crashing below $55,500, but the sell-off is far from settled. More than $2.55 billion in crypto positions were wiped out in 24 hours, with Bitcoin accounting for $1.15 billion, leaving BTC trapped between heavy liquidation zones.Now, traders are wondering: how low can the Bitcoin price go if liquidation continues to grow?

According to the latest CoinGlass data, 361,207 traders were liquidated in 24 hours, with long positions accounting for nearly 89.4% of the $2.55 billion total. Bitcoin alone recorded about $1.15 billion in liquidations, while Ethereum followed with $582.38 million and Solana with nearly $67 million.

The damage is also visible in the derivatives market.

It has been revealed that bitcoin open interest has fallen to around $19.73 billion, while the long/short ratio has dropped to 0.8276. As price fell, leveraged positions were cleared rapidly, leaving fewer traders willing to keep betting on an immediate recovery.

Industry observers note that that concern is now spreading beyond derivatives traders. Robert Kiyosaki, author of Rich Dad Poor Dad, added to the warnings with a blunt post on X,.

He said he would wait for the Bitcoin crash to find a bottom before buying again.

The most key zone is sitting just below Bitcoin’s current price. The liquidation map also indicates a short-position cluster between about $59,326 and $59,863. This creates a clear battle zone.

If Bitcoin breaks back above $59,300, short positions could start getting squeezed, potentially helping BTC recover toward higher levels.

But failure to reclaim that area would leave the market exposed to another move lower.

Below the current price, the next notable support sits around $54,522.

A clean break below that level could bring the $49,011 August 2024 low back into focus.

Could 2027 finally be the year Cardano (ADA) overtakes Ripple (XRP) in the cryptocurrency rankings? Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta AI predicts that, despite XRP’s established position among the industry’s largest digital assets, network upgrades, renewed institutional interest, and a shift in investor sentiment could make it more likely than it first appears.

Both cryptocurrencies have spent years competing for attention, albeit with very different propositions. XRP has built its reputation around cross-border payments and financial infrastructure, while Cardano has focused on research-driven development, decentralized applications, and a carefully structured ecosystem.

Industry observers note that however, market leadership can change quickly during a cryptocurrency bull market. If Cardano delivers on its ambitious development roadmap while XRP struggles to maintain its momentum, the gap between the two could narrow considerably.

And while flipping XRP would require an extraordinary rally, ADA could climb to a valuation few investors currently anticipate.

One of Cardano’s biggest opportunities heading into 2027 is its ongoing push to improve network scalability.

Sources indicate that the planned Ouroboros Leios upgrade is particularly crucial. Designed to increase transaction throughput without compromising Cardano’s decentralized architecture, Leios could address a longstanding criticism: its ability to compete with higher-throughput blockchain ecosystems.

Sources indicate that cardano’s Dijkstra development cycle also introduces further improvements, with Peras activation targeted for the second quarter of 2027. Peras is designed to improve transaction settlement speed by reducing the time needed to achieve stronger confirmation confidence.

Meanwhile, developments around programmable tokens, decentralized finance, and real-world asset tokenization could help Cardano attract applications that generate genuine demand for ADA.

These upgrades won’t automatically translate into higher token prices, but successful implementation could give investors a compelling reason to reconsider Cardano’s long-term valuation.

In a recent development, XRP has several advantages that Cardano cannot easily replicate. Ripple has spent years building relationships across the financial sector, while the XRP Ledger continues to expand into institutional decentralized finance, stablecoins, and tokenized real-world assets.

According to recent reports, the network processed an average of approximately 2.48 million daily transactions during the first quarter of 2026, while its real-world asset market capitalization reached $2.25Bn. These are meaningful indicators of ecosystem activity.

It has been revealed that however, XRP’s enormous market capitalization also creates a challenge for investors seeking outsized returns. With a much larger valuation than ADA, XRP needs substantially more capital inflows to achieve the same percentage gains.

It has been revealed that recent market comparisons have placed XRP’s valuation at roughly ten times Cardano’s, highlighting the scale of the challenge. If capital rotates toward smaller, established layer-1 networks during the next bull market, ADA could benefit disproportionately.

ADA previously reached an all-time high around $3.10 during the 2021 bull market, demonstrating that the cryptocurrency can attract substantial speculative demand when market conditions are favorable.

According to recent reports, A sustained recovery towards its previous peak would be an crucial psychological milestone. However, a genuine breakout beyond that region would potentially open the door to a much larger valuation.

Industry observers note that for XRP, the challenge is maintaining its market leadership while competing with an expanding range of payment-focused blockchain networks. Its established institutional presence provides a strong foundation, but continued adoption growth will be necessary to justify a substantially higher valuation.

The key technical signal to watch for ADA is a sustained sequence of higher highs and higher lows on the weekly and monthly charts, accompanied by improving relative strength against XRP.

A decisive break above previous cycle resistance, followed by a successful retest, could signal that a longer-term trend reversal is underway.

Consider an optimistic scenario in which the broader cryptocurrency market enters another substantial bull phase during 2027.

Cardano successfully implements its major upgrades, DeFi activity expands, institutional interest improves, and investors begin viewing ADA as an undervalued alternative to larger blockchain assets.

Under these circumstances, a move towards $1.50–$2.50 becomes an interesting longer-term price scenario, with the upper end representing a substantial recovery towards its previous all-time high.

At $2.50, Cardano’s market capitalization would approach $95 billion, assuming a circulating supply of approximately 38 billion ADA. That would represent a significant increase from its current valuation.

However, overtaking XRP would depend on more than Cardano’s own performance. XRP’s valuation would also need to be considered, meaning ADA could reach $2.50 without necessarily overtaking its rival.

Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta AI predicts that Cardano has a genuine opportunity to flip XRP in 2027, with ADA potentially reaching $2.50.

Although XRP remains the more established cryptocurrency, Meta AI believes Cardano offers the more interesting upside opportunity if its development roadmap translates into meaningful ecosystem growth.

In a recent development, the deciding factor will be execution. If Leios, Peras, and Cardano’s broader adoption initiatives deliver, 2027 could be the year ADA finally challenges XRP’s dominance.

With a low-upkeep routine of every four to six weeks, using at-home waxing kits is a no-brainer beauty move. After ordering our editor-tested, dermatologist-approved recommendations, keep reading for more expert tips on post-waxing care.

Out of all the different at-home waxing kits we tried, these wax strips were the easiest to use and the most effective at picking up every single little hair. Flamingo's wax strips won our top spot because they were super simple to apply with very little prep work besides getting the area clean and dry. The soft wax strips are infused with soothing ingredients, like castor seed oil and beeswax, making them ideal for removing fine hair on larger areas, like your arms. Best of all, they’re ready to go whenever you are—no microwave is required. To use them, simply peel apart the strip and apply it, rubbing firmly against your skin to make sure it coats every hair.

We did find the strips a little too substantial for areas like the face, but you can always cut them down to the correct size with a pair of scissors. Pulling up the wax strip stung quite a bit for Montemayor, but it was over within seconds and the wax effortlessly removed most of her hair on the first go. The strips are very sticky, so she reapplied it to the same area to ensure every last hair was yanked. She especially likes that the post-wax cloth feels very soothing on the skin, and that it helps remove any excess product and stickiness. Montemayor claims her redness went away after about an hour, and she was hair-free for a good two weeks after that.

Industry observers note that hard wax kits tend to be messy when they’re applied or removed incorrectly. Remember to always apply a thin, even layer and pull the wax in the opposite direction of hair growth for a seamless waxing experience. However, the results are similar to those you would get at a waxing salon. This Sliick kit comes with a silicone cup and spatula, which makes the heating and application process a breeze. It takes a few rounds of heating and stirring the hard wax to get the right consistency. Once it starts looking like caramel, you’re ready to wax—and the waiting window is totally worth it because the hard wax is easy to maneuver and contains antioxidant-rich acai berry.

“Use a new stick each time you dip into the wax pot to avoid introducing bacteria, which could potentially cause infections,” notes Gail Strong, an esthetician and CEO at Invigorate Spa in Indianapolis, Indiana.

The wax itself was easy to spread, but we found that it works best when laid in a thick layer, as thick as a banana peel. Montemayor likes that letting the wax cool completely before pulling the strip gives her a better result. The wax strip came up in one piece, lifting and removing all the hairs in its path. Unlike some of the hard wax kits we tried, this one didn’t leave any wax crumbs behind. Once you’re done waxing, all you have to do is let the wax in the cup and on the applicator dry, and it easily peels off. Montemayor found that after waxing her legs with this kit, it took about 10 days before she noticed the hair growing back.

Pro tip: Remember to dip a fresh stick into the wax pot to avoid introducing bacteria that can cause infections, says Strong.

In a recent development, waxing tends to irritate the skin, but these strips from Billie were the most gentle of all the wax strips we tried. The sticky formula contains added castor oil, avocado oil, and aloe vera to soothe the skin, while the no-rub soft-gel wax attaches to every hair, whether it’s very fine or extra coarse.I used the Billie strips on my legs and underarms, and it was the least painful at-home waxing kit I tried. It’s a little tricky getting all of the hairs of my underarms, but the strips are very sticky, so I can go over the area two or three times and I’m left with smooth, hair-free pits. These strips didn’t leave behind wax on my skin, so cleanup is easy. I’ll just follow up with the included post-wax serum and my redness and minimal irritation are gone.The medium-sized wax strips are great for larger areas like the underarms and legs, but the small strips are too big to use on the upper lip or around the eyebrows. An easy hack is to trim them to fit your face—and with 32 wax strips in total, the $9 kit remains a great value.

Sometimes you just want a product that works for thousands of people. This all-inclusive kit earned a 4.4-star average from more than 38,350 Amazon reviews. More than 26,460 of them were perfect 5-star ratings. Casual.

According to recent reports, so what makes it so impressive among Amazon shoppers? This kit includes quite literally everything you could need for a seamless at-home waxing experience. Waxing beads, an adjustable heat warmer, and 20 sticks for sanitary application? Of course. Skin prep spray and a soothing aftercare spray? Definitely. An instructional booklet with access to advice from a waxing expert via a smartphone app? Yup. It’s like the salon is truly in your bathroom.

Honestly, the biggest con about this device is that it requires some work. You’ve got to plug in the digital wax melt warmer and set the temperature; insert the wax bean bag into the removable waxing pot, and clean up the warmer and spatulas after. But TBH, based on the glowing Amazon reviews it’s a relatively small tradeoff worth the upkeep.

Women with sensitive skin or a low pain tolerance will love this sugaring wax because it’s gentle on the skin without compromising on hair removal. Its screw-on, roll-on applicator makes applying this wax a cinch, allowing you to reach tricky spots, like your chin or underarm, more precisely. You can easily wash the applicator after each use with soap and water. And to nourish the skin, the formula contains 100 percent organic virgin argan oil from Morocco.

Industry observers note that considering the above, it's no surprise that WH contributors love this buy, too. Its compact size is excellent for touch-ups on the go. And it’s a fantastic mess-free alternative that’s easy to apply and smells delicious, says Jackson. Plus, the wax works on shorter hairs as small as two millimeters, so it removes prickly stubble. While she fully recommends this at-home waxing kit, it’s worth noting that it’s not a hard wax, and it comes with cloth strips that may not cling to thicker hair types.

Industry observers note that these Sally Hansen wax strips are infused with vitamin E and avocado oil for a more nourishing and less irritating waxing experience. The full-size strips are still large enough to cover a good amount of ground—like armpits and legs—and can leave you hair-free for up to eight weeks. You can also snip these strips to fit different areas of your face and body, including your underarms and bikini line.

According to recent reports, before Jackson switched over to laser hair removal, she always kept these strips on hand all the time. She used them for years and suggests putting a dish towel in the microwave for 20 seconds and placing the strip in the towel to warm it up before using it for better results. You can also follow up with a separate oil or serum, since it occasionally leaves a sticky residue on the skin that can be uncomfortable.

According to recent reports, these waxing sticks are different from anything else we tried. Despite looking like something you would find in a kid's craft box, these don't play around when it comes to their ability to remove facial hair. The kit comes with two crayon-looking wax sticks, one small and one large. The small one is great for getting the errant hairs around your brows, while the larger stick is the perfect size for removing upper lip hair and peach fuzz on the rest of the face. Montemayor found that the stick made her feel like she had more control over where the wax went, which is especially key in sensitive areas like the face.To heat up the wax, all you need is a hair dryer. We recommend using the wax sticks in a bathroom because you’ll need to reheat the sticks often. The sticks are a little stringy, and the application can get messy because you’re trying to catch the wax and apply it before it continues dripping down the stick.

The hard wax has a pliable texture that snugly fits the curves of your face and can be applied in a nice, thick layer, which makes it easier to remove. We could do two to three swipes with the stick before we needed to blast it with the hair dryer again. The wax formula itself was very gentle and didn’t leave any sticky residue behind or tug at the top layer of skin. Overall, it was mostly painless because you’re working in such small sections. Once the stick dries, you can tuck it away for safekeeping and reuse it again the next time you need to remove your facial hair. We particularly like these sticks because they're travel-friendly, too. You can definitely throw them in a toiletry bag on your next weekend getaway.

With only three key factors to keep in mind, shopping for at-home waxing kits is refreshingly simple.

Before waxing, you should know there are two types of waxes: hard and soft.

If you want to use something stripless, go for hard wax. It adheres to the hair follicle (versus the skin), hardens, and can be removed on its own, eliminating the need for paper strips. For some, it may even feel less painful than soft wax, so it's great for sensitive skin, notes dermatologist Nazanin Saedi, MD. The only caveat is that you may have to apply it several times in the same area to make sure all the hairs you target are removed.

It has been revealed that soft wax, on the other hand, is soft and applied in a thin layer. A paper strip is then used to adhere and remove the wax. Often, the top layer of skin is also removed, so it can be irritating for people with sensitive skin.

In a recent development, ideally, beginners should look for kits that contain everything they need to get the job done—wax, strips, and finishing oil, at minimum. Novices may also appreciate waxing kits that come with pre-loaded strips, since they're less messy and require less precision. The tradeoff? You're limited to the size of the included strips, so look for kits with multiple sizes if you're targeting different areas of the body. Larger strips are fantastic for your legs, while small strips are practical for your face.

Sources indicate that it's key to use the safest and gentlest wax kits available to avoid irritating, burning, and potentially scarring your skin. If you have sensitive skin, look for waxing kits that include skin-soothing ingredients, like castor and almond oils or aloe. And whatever you use, first test the wax in an area on your body that isn't too visible. This will allow you to see if it is gentle enough for your skin. If you experience a bad reaction, you'll know it's time to pivot to a different product.

According to recent reports, for the past year, Women’s Health contributors and I, including Sabrina Talbert, Jasmine Gomez, Danielle Jackson, and Cristina Montemayor, tested the bestselling, most popular, and top-rated at-home waxing kits. Our team consulted dermatologists Blair Murphy-Rose, MD, Nazanin Saedi, MD, and Uchenna Okereke, MD, for pre-waxing advice and aftercare instructions to prevent irritation and promote healthy skin. Then, we got our hands on the kits and tested them in the comfort of our own homes, evaluating attributes like ease of use, comfort, results, and overall value. Of the 25 at-home waxing kits tested, the seven on this list delivered the best results in our in-depth evaluations.

Industry observers note that at-home waxing removes body hair conveniently and cost-effectively, and the best kits do it rapidly while minimizing pain and irritation. So, if you’re ready to ditch the razors, check out this list of the best waxing kits, tested by dermatologists and WH editors.

After waxing, you can prevent ingrown hairs from forming and minimize irritation immediately afterward by applying cool aloe to soothe skin, and sticking to loose clothes that won't create friction. "Aloe vera has anti-inflammatory properties that help soothe sunburned skin, while glycerin specifically can help to boost hydration levels to restore the skin's moisture barrier," dermatologist Divya Shokeen, MD, previously told WH in our guide to the best aloe vera gel. Some kits also come with nourishing oils and wipes to help minimize any post-wax irritation.

Before you head off to wax unwanted hair, these are a few other tips you should keep in mind.

Recent findings suggest that waxing removes hair by lifting it out at the root. With traditional waxing, hot wax is applied to skin and the hair is pulled off in the opposite direction of the way it's growing. The key word here and what can make at-home waxing dangerous is that it's hot.

In a recent development, “Hot wax can burn the skin—and it is a particularly dangerous type of burn because the hot product adheres to the skin,” indicates Dr. Murphy-Rose. Always make sure you're following the heating directions closely and that you hold your hand over the wax after it's been heated to gauge the temperature before applying it to your skin.

In a recent development, then, first test the wax in an area on your body that isn't too visible. "That way you can check the temperature, but also see how your skin reacts," indicates Dr. Saedi. Testing a product will also allow you to see if it is gentle enough for your skin. “It's important to use the safest and gentlest wax kits available to avoid irritating, burning, and potentially scarring your skin," says Dr. Murphy-Rose. You should also avoid any ingredients you have a known allergy or sensitivity to. If you experience a bad reaction, you'll know it's time to pivot to a different product.

"Hot wax tends to adhere the strongest, so while it may remove hairs more efficiently, it can also stick to skin more and pull off those top layers of the skin as it's also pulling out your hair,” states Dr. Murphy-Rose.

Waxing exfoliates the top layer of skin and is more likely to cause hyperpigmentation a.k.a. dark spots, says Dr. Okereke. She says to think of the skin after waxing like a fresh, pink wound. "Ultraviolet rays are attracted to wounds, making the freshly waxed skin more susceptible to darkening as melanin (the dark pigment in skin) floods the area to try and protect it." Luckily, there is a simple fix: Wear broad-spectrum sunscreen! Better yet, keep that new skin out of the sun completely for at least a few days.

Sources indicate that you'll also want to avoid any extra exfoliation, like retinol, chemical peels, and microdermabrasion, a few days prior and a few days following your at-home wax. A few other good things to know before getting started: Always wax on clean skin to avoid bacterial contamination in pores and make sure your hairs are long enough (at least 1/4 of an inch) to be grabbed by the wax.

The key to preventing ingrown hairs (an all too common downside of waxing for many) is to get the full hair follicle. The best way to do this is by keeping your skin taut and pulling the wax strip in the opposite direction of the way that your hair grows.

Sugaring, aka sugared wax or sugar gel, is generally safer because it’s applied to skin at room temperature (read: no risk of burning skin) and warms up with body heat. “Sugared ‘wax’ is not truly wax,” Dr. Murphy-Rose says. Rather, it’s a combination of sugar, lemon juice, and water. Some brands will infuse glycerin, fragrance, honey, or essential oils. Regardless of which brand you opt for, sugaring is water-soluble and easily rinses off the skin compared to hot wax, she says.

Sources indicate that sugaring and threading remove the hair follicle from the root but with less exfoliating, offering a gentler process, Dr. Okereke says. Though she warns that she's also had patients with coily-textured hair that still develop ingrown hairs and scarring from sugaring as well. The bottom line: "If you know you're prone to hyperpigmentation, ingrown hairs, or scarring, see a dermatologist to discuss the best hair removal practices for you," says Dr. Okereke.

Veteran commodity trader Peter Brandt has provided yet another bearish outlook for the world's largest cryptocurrency, arguing that the crypto asset could see much more misery if its historical market trends play out.

Bitcoin Bitcoin Every bull market phase in BTC's history has ended with at least a 75% correction of the previous parabolic bull trend. Could this be what's happening in Bitcoin? https://t.co/PVXJpetSyO.

Brandt's latest doomsday prediction comes at a time when Bitcoin is still trying to recover from its biggest sell-off to date, which has wiped out close to half of its market value from its October 2025 peak.

The trader's latest post on X highlights a pattern he has found throughout Bitcoin's price history: previous bull runs have always ended with devastating market corrections.

"Every bull market phase in the history of BTC has ended with at least a 75% correction of the prior parabolic bull trend," Brandt's X post reads.

Continuing his warning, Brandt raised an alarming question: "Is this what is happening with Bitcoin?".

Sources indicate that the trading veteran has not put a number on the possible crash. But his words point toward the possibility that the current drop in Bitcoin might be part of a larger correction and not just a temporary dip.

A look at Bitcoin's historical crashes could paint a scary picture.

Bitcoin has a history of sharp corrections following major bull runs.

Industry observers note that for example, the crypto asset dropped by around 84% from its December 2017 high to its December 2018 low. Another example of such a deep price correction can be found in the 2022 bear market, when BTC saw a drop of around 77% from its November 2021 all-time high.

These historic crashes have shown the extreme losses that Bitcoin investors have faced during such market corrections.

At the time of writing on Nov. 20, Bitcoin is at the moment trading at around $62,000, which is almost 51% below its October 2025 all-time high.

If it were to undergo a 75% price correction from its all-time high, then it would drop to around $31,550.

But it's worth mentioning that Brandt referred to a correction of the prior parabolic bull trend, which may not be the same as a 75% correction from the peak.

Interestingly enough, this is not the first time the trader has warned about an even darker future for Bitcoin's price.

Industry observers note that earlier, on Nov. 15, Brandt shared a weekly BTC chart showing a potential head-and-shoulders formation, a technical pattern that usually signals a bearish reversal.

According to Brandt, if the pattern is confirmed, there's a chance that Bitcoin could never revisit its previous all-time high in his lifetime.

Industry observers note that the chart he shared also indicates an notable zone between $60,000 and $65,000. A confirmed breakdown below this zone could further strengthen the bearish outlook.

Moreover, there is still plenty of selling pressure in the crypto market. The latest upgrade from Lookonchain on Nov. 19 revealed that U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had seen net outflows of around $975 million over the past seven days. The biggest net outflows came from BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT).

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Recent findings suggest that it’s easy to underrate walking as one of the best things we can do for our fitness—after all, it doesn’t get your heart rate up like running or a HIIT workout. But that doesn’t mean you’re not getting tons of physical and mental health benefits from walking, whether you’re following a walking workout plan or not.

Recent findings suggest that and perhaps one of the best things about walking is that it doesn’t require any specialized equipment or gear except a really good pair of comfy walking shoes. Luckily for you, we’re constantly testing walking shoes, and we’ve narrowed down all the options out there to a list of pairs we reach for again and again. We’ve used our testing experience, plus picked the brains of podiatrists and other experts to compile our favorites in this guide.

If you’ve logged even a couple of miles in a not-so-great pair of walking shoes, you know wearing the wrong footwear can make what started out as a nice walk turn into an uncomfortable slog fast (we’re talking blisters, achy arches, plantar fasciitis, and more).

It has been revealed that the right walking shoes, on the other hand, can help you walk farther, feel happier while doing it, and gush to friends about your sneakers (ask us how we know). Plus, select styles can help prevent injury or overpronation (when your arches collapse and cause your foot to angle inward), says podiatrist Chanel Perkins, DPM, an assistant professor of foot and ankle podiatry in the Department of Orthopedic Surgery and Rehabilitation at the University of Texas Medical Branch.

After testing dozens of walking shoes for our 2026 Fitness Awards, the Adrenaline GTS 25 took the top spot for its near-perfect balance between cushioning and stability. Our staffers who tested it say it’s comfortable enough to walk in for hours. “It offers just the right amount of cushioning for a bouncy step without compromising on support for my flat, wide feet,” claims WH beauty editor Nicole Saunders.

According to recent reports, that comfort starts with the 25’s updated midsole, which feels plusher than previous models without losing an ounce of stability. It still features the brand’s signature GuardRails technology—firmer along the sides and softer through the center—to gently lock in your stride. In our testing, Brooks continues to set the standard for stability, making this a standout pick for anyone whose feet tend to roll inward while walking.

According to recent reports, when it comes to fit, the 25 has a roomier toe box up front and a secure (but still comfortable) heel lock back, which helps cut down on friction and lowers your chances of blisters during long walks. The higher 10 mm drop creates a slightly forward-leaning stride that takes pressure off the calves and Achilles, making the 25 a smart pick for anyone with tight lower legs or Achilles sensitivity. If you prefer a flatter feel underfoot, though, we recommend something lower profile like the Hoka Mach 6.

At 9.5 ounces, it’s one of the heavier options on this list, but that added weight comes from the stability tech and structured testing. We barely noticed the difference, especially once we got moving.

According to recent reports, pidich loves that the design encourages great form—the sole ensures that your feet rock off the ground rather than push off your toes. Rogers specifically recommends the shoe for her plantar fasciitis (a condition where you feel pain in the arch) patients for this exact reason. “The lightweight feel on this shoe propels feet forward rather than making them do extra work,” she claims.

WH style editor Shannon Zitz found in her testing that the foam absorbed impact well on both pavement and the treadmill. “My feet—unfortunately plagued by plantar fasciitis—never felt fatigued wearing this shoe,” she mentioned, noting that her stride felt smooth and natural.

The Clifton 11 is available in wide and extra-wide sizing, making it a good fit for a wide variety of walkers.

I’ve been wearing this shoe nonstop with capris, leggings, and athletic shorts.”.

The Upcoming Balance 608 V5 Trainer has over 38,000 reviews on Amazon, and for good reason. The brand integrated its signature ABZORB midsole (a blend of substantial foam cushioning with compression resistance), which is designed to lessen the blow on joints when walking.

Industry observers note that the 608 has tons of shock absorption which makes it great for neutral to high arches. But since it lacks stability features, it’s not our top choice for flat feet. We do like that it comes in narrow, standard, and wide sizing.

Ideally, walking shoes will assist with your gait (your walking pattern) instead of just cushioning impact. Your shoe should also be somewhat stiff—the more it bends, the less stability it will have.

According to recent reports, to test the flexibility, hold the shoe at the toe box and heel counter and try to fold the shoe in half by pushing on its ends to see how sturdy it is. If it folds in half or twists with ease, it’s too flexible, says podiatrist Elizabeth Daughtry, MD, a podiatrist and foot and ankle specialist with Foot and Ankle Specialists of the Mid-Atlantic in Cary, North Carolina.

She also adds that seeking out a shoe with a boat-like (rockered) shape, rigid midsole, and firm heel counter can help stabilize feet, control overpronation (collapsing arches), and prevent heel striking.

In a recent development, look for walking shoes that have an outsole with more rigidity in the midsole for stability. Different feet have different needs, so it’s important to have insoles that can be removed in case you use orthotics. “Most shoes don’t offer adequate support alone,” says Dr. Daughtry. “You should supplement most shoes with a more custom-molded orthotic, which your local podiatrist can make for you, as this provides adequate support and helps with shock absorption, while also allowing for additional cushioning.”.

It has been revealed that testing footwear is something we’re a little obsessive about, and we’re testing walking shoes on a constant basis. Over the past year alone, we’ve tested over 100 walking shoes, paying attention to fit, comfort, support, and durability. To narrow it down even further, we also consulted podiatrists and certified trainers about their favorite picks.

Enjin Matrixchain Votes on OpenGov Today: What Changes for ENJ Holders on November 16

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1550 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Enjin holders vote through November 13 on moving Matrixchain to OpenGov on November 16.
  • Enjin's newly introduced proposal deposit sounds steep at 1,000 ENJ.
  • According to recent reports, enjin holders have until today, November 13, to vote on moving the Matrixchain to the Fort Canning release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Enjin holders vote through November 13 on moving Matrixchain to OpenGov on November 16. Here is how the nine tracks, the 1,000 ENJ deposit and conviction voting work, and what the Relaychain vote shows.

Enjin's newly introduced proposal deposit sounds steep at 1,000 ENJ. It's actually the cheap part.

According to recent reports, enjin holders have until today, November 13, to vote on moving the Matrixchain to the Fort Canning release. The referendum opened November 10. If it passes, the upgrade is targeted for November 16 at block #12,319,600, with the network moving from runtime 1.3.1 to 1.4.3. Enjin's Fort Canning announcement lays out the plan, and the official changelog carries the technical detail.

Sources indicate that the Relaychain has already made the jump. Referendum #16 approved its upgrade on October 28, and it went live on November 9. The Matrixchain vote is the second half of one upgrade, and it is the half that changes how Matrixchain makes decisions from then on.

Sources indicate that early coverage reported the schedule and the headline numbers: nine tracks, 1,000 ENJ. The changelog and the governance portal show the mechanics behind them, and those mechanics change more than the headlines suggest.

Today, the Matrixchain runs its governance through the older Democracy, Council and Technical Committee pallets, the modules that handle proposals and votes. Fort Canning replaces all three with a latest set: Referenda, Conviction Voting, Origins, Whitelist and the Enjin Fellowship. Under OpenGov, any account can submit a referendum on one of nine tracks, and from the moment the upgrade lands, Matrixchain's own upgrades go through that process.

A track is a lane for a particular kind of decision. Enjin's changelog describes the families: Root and the admin tracks for the highest-stakes changes, Whitelisted Caller for proposals the Fellowship fast-tracks, and two special tracks, Referendum Killer and Referendum Canceller, for stopping a proposal that shouldn't proceed. Matrixchain gets no treasury tracks: those, sized by how much a proposal would spend, stay on the Relaychain, where treasury requests now go. Each track has its own deposit, approval curve and enactment period, and the Enjin Fellowship can fast-track time-sensitive proposals.

Recent findings suggest that splitting decisions this way means a small treasury request doesn't face the same bar as a change to the chain's core. Riskier tracks demand larger deposits and more support, while smaller ones move faster and cost less.

In a recent development, the submission deposit rises from 0.025 ENJ to 1,000 ENJ on every track, a 40,000-fold increase. The deposit is refunded when a referendum passes or is canceled, and it exists to deter spam. As an illustration, using the roughly $66 million market cap reported in early October, ENJ traded near three cents, which would put 1,000 ENJ around $33.

That is only the entry ticket. The cost that matters comes next. A referendum also needs a decision deposit before it moves into voting, and the changelog lists steep figures: 2,500,000 ENJ on Root and Fellowship Admin, 1,000,000 ENJ on the other admin tracks, and 2,500 to 250,000 ENJ on the Relaychain's treasury tracks. At the same illustrative price, the 2.5 million ENJ Root deposit comes to roughly $80,000, about 0.12% of the 2.02 billion ENJ total issuance.

Industry observers note that so proposing is cheap, and pushing a proposal through is not. Anyone can raise an idea, but anyone who wants the network to vote on something big needs real stake in the outcome. The changelog indicates the same values apply on both chains, and Matrixchain adopts them for its latest tracks.

Industry observers note that the best evidence of how these votes work comes from the Relaychain referendum that has already finished. Enjin's governance portal highlights referendum #16 as finalised, approved on October 28 and enacted on November 9.

In a recent development, the final tally on the page is small. Eleven voters cast 381,303.02 ENJ of conviction-weighted voting power, and all of it went to Aye: 100% in favor, 0 ENJ against. The page also reveals raw, unweighted support of 271,303.2 ENJ, which it describes as the total balance backing the proposal and the figure the support curve uses. The conviction multiplier on the page runs from under 1x up to 6x.

Two numbers stand out. First, an entire chain upgrade passed with 271,303 ENJ of raw support, about 0.013% of the 2.02 billion ENJ total issuance, a figure worked out from the portal's number. Second, conviction added about 110,000 ENJ of weight on top of the raw balance, an average multiplier of roughly 1.4x. Voters picked up some extra weight, but most didn't lock their tokens for the long periods that earn the top multipliers.

Industry observers note that A 100% Aye result claims little by itself. A scheduled upgrade with no organized opposition passes easily, and the tally indicates how thin engagement was.

Fort Canning adds the safeguard that thin turnout calls for. A referendum now needs a minimum share of total ENJ voting in support. The changelog sets 0.5% on Root and the admin tracks, 0.005% to 0.125% on the Relaychain's treasury tracks, 0.1% for Referendum Killer and 0.05% for Referendum Canceller. Measured against 2.02 billion ENJ, that means about 10.1 million ENJ on Root, roughly 101,000 to 2.5 million on the treasury tracks, about 2.02 million to kill a referendum and about 1.01 million to cancel one.

In a recent development, referendum #16's 271,303 ENJ of raw support would clear the lowest treasury floor of about 101,000 ENJ, but it would miss the Root floor by a factor of about 37. The page doesn't show which track the referendum used, and a runtime upgrade typically sits on a high-stakes track, so the Root comparison works as an illustration and not as a finding. The floors also didn't exist when #16 passed, since Fort Canning introduced them.

In a recent development, that is the real change. Under the fresh rules, 11 wallets can't carry a chain-level decision on their own. Low turnout means failure, and proposals that matter will need far more ENJ behind them. Enjin's changelog says Matrixchain upgrades go through OpenGov starting with this one, which suggests today's vote still runs on the current system, so the floors will first bite on the first OpenGov referendum.

According to recent reports, holders who haven't voted can still do so through Enjin's governance portal before the window closes. Voting locks tokens, so the lock length is worth checking first. Enjin's support article on voting explains the trade-off: the longer the lock, the more a vote counts, and tokens stay locked until the period ends.

According to recent reports, node operators on the Matrixchain can wait for the result before upgrading, as Enjin has indicated, and then follow the changelog for the version to install. Relaychain operators already needed client version 1.8.1.

This vote is more about control than speed. OpenGov spreads decisions across tracks with deposits and support floors built for the weight of each choice, and it moves ENJ holders from voting on a handful of items to a standing governance system. The Relaychain's first vote revealed how little participation it took under the old rules, and the first referenda after November 16 will show whether holders turn out for the new ones. If most proposals stall at the decision deposit, the system costs too much. If they clear with a handful of voters, the floors aren't doing their job. Either result will tell holders what their ENJ can do.

The economist shared a video with a very alarming headline: "The Next Crash Will Be Worse Than 2008.".

In one of his most recent posts on X, Schiff argued that the recent gold price downtrend might signal a grim outlook for other key asset classes.

Sources indicate that "It's probably a bad sign that gold is falling this much. It probably means that the stock and real estate markets are going to fall even more in percentage terms," Schiff cautioned.

Industry observers note that according to Peter Schiff, gold's recent price behavior could be signaling deflation. As a result, this might lead to a more severe financial crisis.

However, Peter Schiff is convinced that the Federal Reserve will step in to prevent this financial apocalypse.

"Gold is signaling deflation. But asset deflation would bust the government and the banking system, so the Fed will pivot to avoid it," the economist explained.

Simply put, Schiff assumes that the Federal Reserve will pivot and introduce monetary stimulus to prevent a financial meltdown.

In another startling prediction, the economist warned that the U.S. stock market might wipe out all its gains since President Donald Trump took office.

"There's a good chance that the U.S. stock market is about to give back all the gains since Trump took office," the economist predicted.

Bitcoin (BTC) price continues to fall as the sell-off from the $86,000 - $87,000 region in October is gathering momentum. The sell-off has accelerated in recent days, and BTC price has slipped to roughly $61,900, moving closer to the next technical support level at $60,000.

Industry observers note that the daily chart highlights several concerning technical developments for Bitcoin. Shorter-term moving averages continue to fall below longer-term moving averages, forming a technical pattern commonly known as a death cross. The death cross has now formed twice with 100 and 200 EMAs, indicating a worsening technical setup for Bitcoin, commonly known as a double death cross.

Several key moving averages continue to cluster in the $75,000 - $76,000 region, adding resistance for Bitcoin price action.

Relative Strength Index (RSI) has started to move closer to the oversold region, indicating that momentum has started to slow for Bitcoin.

Industry observers note that taken together, this technical setup indicates that selling pressure for Bitcoin has been increasing on multiple time frames. We are monitoring $60,000 as a key support level. This level was also an area of interest for buyers during the June correction in Bitcoin.

Should BTC price continue to move lower and break out below $60,000, the next level of support to watch will be $58,000, followed by $56,000.

For Bitcoin price to reverse course and show signs of a meaningful short-term rebound, it will need to continue higher and break out above $64,000 - $65,000.

Sources indicate that breaking out above $68,000 would be a strong move that could help to stabilize Bitcoin in the short term. A positive move for Bitcoin would need to continue higher and reclaim several key moving averages. Until then, Bitcoin will continue to trade in a more bearish technical setup.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stock market crash fears intensify as Nasdaq plunges 10% and S&P 500 drops 8.6% in its worst week since April 2025.
  • Dow and S&P 500 enter correction territory, falling more than 10% from their record highs as Wall Street's sell-off accelerates.
  • AI and semiconductor stocks lead the crash, with Nvidia, AMD, Micron and other technology stocks facing heavy losses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stock market crash fears intensify as Nasdaq plunges 10% and S&P 500 drops 8.6% in its worst week since April 2025.

Dow and S&P 500 enter correction territory, falling more than 10% from their record highs as Wall Street's sell-off accelerates.

AI and semiconductor stocks lead the crash, with Nvidia, AMD, Micron and other technology stocks facing heavy losses.

The US stock market crash intensified this week as investors aggressively dumped technology and artificial intelligence stocks, pushing major Wall Street indexes toward their steepest weekly declines in years. The Nasdaq Composite plunged approximately 10%, marking its worst week since the March 2020 pandemic crash, while the S&P 500 lost 8.6%.

Both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones entered correction territory, raising concerns that the AI-driven market rally may be facing a deeper repricing.

With technology stocks leading the decline, investors are now questioning whether the latest stock market crash signals a temporary correction or the beginning of a broader downturn.

Wall Street’s losses accelerated on Friday, with major indexes closing sharply lower after another wave of selling hit AI and semiconductor stocks.

On Friday, the S&P 500 fell 3.7% to close at 6,910.39, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.28% to 22,617.73. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 949 points, closing at 48,147.33.

This is the WORST WEEK for the STOCK MARKET since March 2020Nasdaq 100: -5.6% today, -10.4% this week, worst since 2020.S&P 500: -3.7% today, -8.6% this week, its worst week since April 2025Semiconductors: -10.7% today, -17.1% this week, worst since 2001 pic.twitter.com/2Z9gqG5Ype.

The S&P 500 and Dow are now more than 10% below their recent record highs, confirming corrections in both indexes. The Nasdaq has also erased its gains for 2026.

The latest stock market crash is primarily driven by growing concerns surrounding the artificial intelligence trade. Investors have poured enormous capital into AI infrastructure, chipmakers and data-center companies.

Sources indicate that however, rising valuations and uncertainty over whether AI investments can generate sufficient returns are prompting investors to reassess the sector’s growth expectations. The sell-off intensified following the market’s reaction to Anthropic’s public debut, which failed to restore confidence in AI stocks. Investors also remain concerned about interest rates, inflation and the possibility of tighter monetary conditions.

The result has been a sharp unwinding of crowded technology trades, with losses spreading beyond individual AI companies into the broader stock market.

Sources indicate that semiconductor stocks have suffered the most severe losses as investors reduce exposure to AI-related companies. Nvidia fell approximately 23% for the week, marking its worst weekly performance since 2008. AMD lost around 20.5%, while Micron and other chipmakers also faced significant selling pressure.

The semiconductor sector’s 17.1% weekly decline highlights the scale of the repricing underway in the AI trade. Companies that previously drove Wall Street’s rally are now becoming the biggest contributors to the market’s losses.

The immediate outlook for Wall Street remains uncertain. The latest correction has raised concerns about valuations, AI spending and investor positioning, but a correction does not automatically signal a prolonged bear market.

Industry observers note that investors will closely watch whether technology stocks stabilize, whether volatility eases and whether companies can deliver earnings growth strong enough to justify their valuations. For now, the stock market crash has exposed the risks of Wall Street’s heavy dependence on AI stocks.

If selling continues across semiconductor and technology companies, the broader market could remain under pressure heading into the next trading week.

"Rich Dad Poor Dad" author Robert Kiyosaki wrote on X on Nov. 20 that he is "most excited about Bitcoin's crash" and is "waiting to buy more." On the same day, Bitcoin was trading at $61,666, more than 50% below its October 2025 peak of about $126,000.

Recent findings suggest that gold fell 1.24% to $3,579 an ounce, and silver lost 0.95% to $42.42, according to TradingView data. The S&P 500 dropped 2.02% on the same day.

Recent findings suggest that kiyosaki started his post with a question. "CRASH: Good or Bad? Gold, silver, Bitcoin, crashing. Weak hands selling. Strong hands waiting to buy?" he wrote.

According to Kiyosaki, the reasons include "incompetence in FED, Banks, and Bond markets." He also wrote that America's debt is "only to grow bigger" as "Banksters steal our wealth via their system legally.".

Industry observers note that the author pointed to Bitcoin's fixed supply. There will be only 21 million BTC in total, and about 20 million coins have already been mined, Kiyosaki wrote. "As far as I know, there has never been a 'money' such as Bitcoin ever before," he added.

According to recent reports, "With price of Bitcoin crashing, I can't wait to buy more coins… just because only 21 million are ever to be mined. It could be a 'nothing burger'…. or the best money I've ever spent," Kiyosaki wrote.

According to recent reports, in late August, Kiyosaki stated on podcasts that he owed creditors $1.2 billion. His ex-wife and business partner, Kim Kiyosaki, later said that the figure covered the loans of a partnership that owns about 1,500 rental units. "We have a lot of apartment houses with our partners," she said.

According to Kim Kiyosaki, Robert Kiyosaki's own share of the debt is $30 million to $60 million. Each of their real estate investments is held in a separate LLC. Robert Kiyosaki also commented on the debt at the time. "If it all comes to hell, you can talk to my attorney," he stated.

In 2012, Kiyosaki's company Rich Global LLC filed for bankruptcy after a court ordered it to pay about $24 million.

There are no pockets at the legs or in the waistband of these leggings, so if you don’t need storage, these are a great option.

Unlike the lulu pair on this list, these have less compression, which I prefer for low-impact workouts. They don’t squeeze too much or make my skin bunch up, so I can move freely and comfortably in any move.

And, the pockets in these leggings come in handy post-workout when you’re off running errands and need an easy place to store your key, credit card, or AirPods. But, they don’t add much width to the hips and have a flattering fit, which isn’t always the case with leggings with pockets. During testing, I found that these literally feel like a second skin—they are so soft and lightweight. Because they’re low compression, they’re also super comfortable for lounging.

Like the Rhone leggings, these are treated with UPF 40, so I like to wear them out for long walks on sunny days because they provide a solid extra layer of sun protection. And, if it really starts to get warm out, they have a quick-drying fabric that’s made with a high nylon content. However, stylist Rose Lauture states that although sweat stains fade quickly, she does notice they show easily in the leggings' lighter colors.

Of all the leggings I've tested, Spanx has the best smoothing fabric. They’re not super compressive (which is why I love them for low-impact exercises), but the fabric is insanely soft, sweat-wicking, and buttery smooth.

In a recent development, “Just like the brand's famed shapewear, these are super flattering, with light stomach compression that snatches your waist, and a back waistband design that slightly dips down to enhance the shape of your booty,” says Wohlner. Their lack of a front seam also makes them much more flattering and so easy to style with anything from a sports bra to a cropped sweater.

I’ve tried a high-intensity workout in these leggings and didn’t feel super supported, so if you’re looking for a pair that can hold you in during deep squats and burpees, these are not my strongest recommendation.

Alo's High-Waist Airbrush Leggings are super versatile because they’re nice and compressive for the gym, and their sleek look plays well with all my casual fits for a chic brunch look.

I’ve struggled to find a pair of high-waisted compression leggings that actually stay up, but these never roll down when I’m moving or sitting, which I appreciate. Plus, they’re on the thinner side, so they don’t feel constrictive like a sausage casing. They stay where I want them for my entire workout and never make me feel claustrophobic.Another pro? The soft material, which has a super smooth, matte look that makes them a bit dressier. Even with sneakers and a zip-up, I find that these make my gym fits look super chic. I deem these leggings worth the buy because of how versatile they are, but shelling out $118 is no easy spend for leggings. So, I like to keep my eye out for a sale where I can get these leggings at a discount.My only gripe is that they run small. I’d recommend sizing up for a more comfortable fit—otherwise, they might feel too tight and could end up rolling down.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BlackRock, the leading asset management firm and Bitcoin’s largest ETF issuer, sparked discussions earlier today following a massive Bitcoin sale by the manufacturer.

The latest data showcased by SosoValue shows that the leading Bitcoin fund has witnessed massive single-day withdrawals from investors who have ventured into its Bitcoin investment product.

Earlier today, BlackRock sold over half a billion dollars’ worth of Bitcoin after its spot Bitcoin ETF, also known as iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), recorded a total of $541.08 million in net outflows.

This massive outflow has come as Bitcoin’s price decline continues to intensify, causing investors to aggressively pull their money out of the fund amid growing market fear.

While this marks the third time this week that BlackRock has recorded a net outflow amid persistent market volatility, it also marks the largest single-day outflow BlackRock has recorded since its launch.

Apparently, the record-breaking withdrawal that the fund just witnessed suggests that institutional and traditional investors are becoming less willing to retain their exposure to Bitcoin through asset managers, especially as Bitcoin’s price continues to slump further.

Although BlackRock has just suffered the largest withdrawal since it debuted its Bitcoin investment product, the record outflow did not alter its dominance in the market.

Further data shows that the BlackRock spot Bitcoin ETF still boasts a massive $47.82 billion in assets under management, spotlighting its leadership in the Bitcoin ETF market.

This positions it far ahead of Fidelity, which ranks as the second-largest Bitcoin ETF with just $10.62 billion in net assets.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • he exploit targeted Chainflip’s cryptographic signing system rather than a smart contract bug.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chainflip lost nearly $4.86 million after an attacker drained its Ethereum vault.

he exploit targeted Chainflip’s cryptographic signing system rather than a smart contract bug.

The latest incident marks Chainflip’s second major security breach in just over two months.

Recent findings suggest that chainflip, a decentralized cross-chain swap protocol, has faced another security scare after nearly $4.86 million in crypto was drained from its Ethereum vault in a single transaction. The attacker moved the stolen funds through Tornado Cash within just nine minutes, forcing the protocol to halt deposits, withdrawals, and swaps.

While its team investigates how the funds were taken.

On-chain investigations by Bitquery show that the attacker targeted Chainflip’s cryptographic key system rather than exploiting a bug in its smart contracts.

It has been revealed that the attacker first obtained a valid Schnorr signature from the Ethereum Vault’s Threshold Signature Scheme (TSS) aggregate key. This allowed the attacker to pass the vault’s normal signature checks.

Recent findings suggest that on November 21, 2026, a newly funded wallet (0x78fa) called the Vault.transferBatch function. The transaction passed verification and drained all the vault’s available funds in a single move.

The attacker then moved swiftly to hide the stolen funds. Within nine minutes, the exploiter swapped the 3,249,631.41 USDC and 758,141.33 USDT for 2,909 ETH (worth around $4.86 million), then sent it to Tornado Cash in 38 separate batches.

Industry observers note that chainflip has not yet confirmed the $4.86 million loss. Instead, the protocol remarked it was aware of a potential exploit affecting its vaults and moved into full safe mode as a precaution.

In a recent development, we’re aware of a potential exploit affecting Chainflip vaults.As a precaution, the protocol is being put into full safe mode. Deposits, withdrawals, swaps and quoting are disabled.We’re investigating and will share updates here as we learn more.

“Deposits, withdrawals, swaps, and quoting are disabled; we’re investigating and will share updates here as we learn more.”.

This is Chainflip’s second major attack in just over two months. On September 12, 2026, the protocol lost $736,442 in a separate exploit targeting its TRON integration. That attack was caused by a software flaw in how Chainflip processed TRON transaction data, while the November 21 attack targeted its Ethereum Vault’s cryptographic signing key.

After the September attack, Chainflip paused TRON swaps and used its surplus reserves to fully reimburse affected liquidity providers in USDC.

The protocol has yet to confirm whether it will follow the same recovery plan for the latest $4.86 million loss.

NEAR’s Inflation Cut: The Math Behind a 5.27% to 3.37% Staking Yield

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1298 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months.
  • Sources indicate that most headlines on NEAR’s new inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number.
  • House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Industry observers note that HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. The cap formula, the epoch step and the yield math show what that does to stakers.

Sources indicate that most headlines on NEAR’s new inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number. They earn about 5.27% today and will earn roughly 3.37% once the cut finishes, and a single line of arithmetic accounts for the gap.

House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto. The proposal touches one parameter, the maximum annual issuance rate, which drops from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. It is the second cut in just over a year, coming after the October 2025 halving from 5%.

Everything else stays put. Issuance still splits 90% to staking participants and 10% to the protocol treasury. There is no new spending program, no validator subsidy and no automatic trigger that could push issuance back up. The full proposal models 11.8 million NEAR of issuance avoided over two years and 66.1 million over six, measured against leaving the cap at 2.5%.

The schedule is a straight line with no stair steps:.

cap(t) = 2.5% − 0.9% × min(t, 24) / 24.

According to recent reports, here t is the number of months since the reduction begins. The 0.9% is the total drop (2.5 minus 1.6), and dividing it by 24 gives a monthly step of 0.0375 percentage points, or 3.75 basis points. The min(t, 24) term caps the ramp at month 24, and the cap sits at 1.6% from there on.

In a recent development, NEAR applies the step every epoch rather than once a month. An epoch lasts about 12 hours, so the cap slips by roughly 0.0006 percentage points each time, far too little to notice on any given day. There are no step dates to mark on a calendar. Sampled every six months, the line looks like this:.

According to recent reports, the yield column uses the math in the next section. It drops about 0.08 percentage points a month, evenly, with no cliff.

Recent findings suggest that new tokens go mostly to stakers, so the staked pool splits the reward, and a smaller pool earns more per token. That gives a working formula:.

gross yield ≈ 0.9 × issuance cap ÷ staking ratio.

Industry observers note that the 0.9 is the staker share of issuance. Using the proposal’s figures, 0.9 × 2.5% ÷ 0.4271 comes to 5.27%, where 42.71% is the staking ratio reported when the proposal went to vote. Put in the 1.6% cap and 0.9 × 1.6% ÷ 0.4271 gives 3.37%, the same number the proposal publishes. Anyone can check the headline yields on a calculator.

According to recent reports, the formula has two limits. It uses the cap, but realized issuance runs a little lower because transaction fees are burned. HSP-029 measured 2.45% in September, which puts today’s yield near 5.16%. The staking ratio also moves. When more people stake, the same rewards spread over more tokens and yield falls further, and when people unstake it climbs. The 3.37% figure assumes today’s ratio holds.

Stakers feel it first. By the proposal’s own math, someone staking 1,000 NEAR ends up with about 20 fewer tokens after two years than if the cap had stayed at 2.5%. The numbers back that up: yield averages about 4.32% across the ramp, roughly 0.95 points under today’s rate for two years.

Industry observers note that holders who don’t stake come out ahead. More than half of NEAR’s supply sits unstaked, and every fresh token dilutes those holdings. Trimming the cap by 0.9 percentage points trims that dilution by the same amount each year. Stakers give up some reward so that everyone else gives up less value.

Validators get an easier path than in 2025, when the halving cut staking rewards from about 9% to 4.75% in a single upgrade. Operators now have 24 months to plan. NEAR’s analysis finds that most validator revenue comes from commission on delegated stake, so service quality and fee competition shape income more than the issuance rate does.

It has been revealed that recent history explains the setup. When the 2025 halving shipped, an earlier community poll had missed the two-thirds threshold, and critics mentioned the core team pushed the change through anyway. HSP-029 sidesteps that argument by design.

It has been revealed that two separate approvals are required. Token holders voting through veNEAR set the direction, and that vote closed November 2 with 99.96% in favor and none against. Validators then decide on their own whether to adopt the protocol upgrade that makes the cap binding. The author, Sal Ternullo of SVRN, opened discussion on October 7, and the process ran through the Screening Committee and Security Council in public. Raising issuance again would take a upcoming proposal and another round of validator adoption, so nothing can be added quietly later.

In a recent development, ratification does not change issuance yet. A one-quarter grace period comes first, giving wallets, exchanges, custodians and staking providers time to patch their disclosures. NEAR One then releases the upgrade and validators choose whether to adopt it, with the reduction starting about a quarter after ratification. On schedule, that means a start in early 2027 and a 1.6% cap around early 2029.

In a recent development, three things are worth tracking. Validator adoption of the upgrade comes first, because the cap stays at 2.5% until enough validators run it. The staking ratio comes next, since it moves yield regardless of the formula. Last are the quarterly transparency reports NEAR has promised, which compare realized issuance with the schedule.

In a recent development, price is a separate question. Lower issuance eases supply pressure, but nothing in it creates demand. The cap will follow its published line down, and yield will follow the cap.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov. 17, according to XRPScan data. As of Nov. 20, 2026, Single Asset Vault (XLS-65) had 25 votes, and Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and the LendingProtocolV1_1 patch had 24 votes each.

In a recent development, XRPScan data shows that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept. 29, 2026, when it came with the v3.4.0 release. According to the patch's voting history, it had about 19 votes for most of October. It started to gain votes again in late October. XRP was trading at $0.96 on Friday.

Lending is built directly into the XRP Ledger's code, with no third-party smart contracts. According to Ripple, lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital "to issue loans and track repayments onchain.".

The model is close to how banks lend. Loans have fixed terms and a repayment schedule, and credit brokers vet borrowers before the loans are issued. On Nov. 19, Clearpool showed the full lending flow on the XRPL Devnet with Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin. In the demo, "An approved lender funds a private vault, and a borrower accepts and repays a loan underwritten offchain by a broker," Clearpool wrote.

According to recent reports, through Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), XRP holders will be able to deposit their coins into shared liquidity pools, and institutional borrowers will take loans from those pools at a fixed rate. After the loan is repaid, "the lender redeems at a higher share price," according to the Clearpool demo.

The amendments still need more votes before they can activate. "An amendment needs more than 80% support, held for 14 days, to activate," XRPScan states on its amendment pages. For the current set of 35 validators, the site puts the threshold at "more than 80% of 35 votes, so 29 needed.".

Dogecoin has shaved about 9% off its futures-to-spot volume ratio over 24 hours, suggesting that risk-off tendencies are taking over investors’ desire to expose themselves to volatility.

According to CoinGlass, futures traded at about eight times spot volume on November 20. The previous 24-hour reading was closer to 8.8 times spot.

Futures quite often precede a pickup in volatility. A reduction in futures positions suggests a way calmer market dynamic, as fewer leveraged positions are there to amplify price moves. Open interest fell 2.25% over the same window. Spot turnover grew faster than futures turnover, which explains why the ratio went down while trading picked up in both markets.

In a recent development, coinGlass still recorded around $4.4 million in net spot selling. Futures saw around $1.4 million in net buying, even as the total value of open positions declined. The market may be taking some risk off, and spot sellers still have the upper hand. CoinGlass volume and flows.

Recent findings suggest that from the price standpoint, things aren’t looking that great. Dogecoin is most likely going to invalidate the $0.057 level on a daily close, after already slipping to around $0.0566 intraday. It closed around $0.0574 on the Binance chart after the November 14 sell-off. The low from that session was around $0.0554, which is where the market could look for support again.

The breakdown below $0.057 is unlikely to be critical on its own. There’s barely enough volume on the market right now to create conditions for a substantial drop. Unfortunately, it brings no positivity whatsoever. On Binance, daily spot volume was down to around $21.5 million on November 19, from $78.6 million during that sell-off.

Recent findings suggest that the technical picture is still bearish. Volume is descending and RSI is back in oversold territory, as it was on November 14. The daily reading is closer to 26 now, compared with around 20 then. The 26-day EMA is also moving down below its longer-term counterparts, hinting at a continuation of the currently bearish trend.

The local decline in volume is unlikely to help the price in the medium to long term, and the possibility of the trend aggravating is still there.

  • Industry observers note that italy’s largest banking group, Intesa Sanpaolo, increased its spot altcoin ETF holdings according to a new disclosure.
  • The bank’s disclosed crypto ETF holdings grew in Q3 2026 to $108.56 million, up $17 million, while digital asset prices moved sideways.
  • Bitcoin, the largest asset in the portfolio, was reduced to make room for altcoins in a possible bid to diversify assets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that italy’s largest banking group, Intesa Sanpaolo, increased its spot altcoin ETF holdings according to a new disclosure. This follows capital rotation out of Bitcoin products by a slew of traditional firms amid dwindling market sentiment.

The bank’s disclosed crypto ETF holdings grew in Q3 2026 to $108.56 million, up $17 million, while digital asset prices moved sideways. In June, total assets were worth $90 million as it looked to diversify and grow holdings systematically.

Bitcoin, the largest asset in the portfolio, was reduced to make room for altcoins in a possible bid to diversify assets. At the end of Q2, BTC holdings stood at $69.32 million but dropped slightly to above $61 million last quarter. The firm’s Ethereum exposure also dropped to $5 million.

In a recent development, however, Solana and XRP products filled the vacuum, highlighting institutional appetite for these assets. At the time of writing, the bank’s spot Solana ETF exposure is at $14.1 million after its investment in the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF ballooned from seven shares to 875,407 shares.

In a recent development, intesa’s XRP investment also grew over the same period to $27.2 million, driven mainly by 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF. The company’s shares in the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF remained unchanged across both quarters.

More broadly, the bank reduced its Bitcoin ETF exposure and increased SOL and XRP products. Most experts believe it follows the current market trend, and firms, especially traditional companies, need to diversify to make up for Bitcoin’s decline.

Historically, during bear phases, there’s a huge rotation of capital into altcoins, though it’s not sustained for long. As expected, Solana and XRP become institutional favorites, while Ethereum trades similarly to Bitcoin.

Industry observers note that the former have the potential to record spikes within the red wave, like in 2022 before the approval of spot ETF products in the United States. These products opened up digital assets to a fresh stash of traditional capital.

Industry observers note that intesa and other banks have since increased their crypto exposure, driven by the need to diversify assets and a broader adoption spree. Heightened institutional and retail interests pushed Bitcoin to an all-time high above $125k last year. Currently, BTC trades at $63,819, while Ethereum is slightly below $1,800.

In a new announcement, major crypto exchange Binance says it will launch an airdrop campaign rewarding all eligible users who hold Ripple USD (RLUSD) on its platform. Eligible users will share rewards from a grand prize pool of 600,000 XRP.

In its statement, Binance stated that eligible incremental RLUSD holdings may qualify for up to a 1.3× reward multiplier, with APRs updated weekly. The campaign will run from today, November 11, 2026, to December 18, 2026, at 00:00 (UTC).

In a recent development, share 600,000 XRP by holding RLUSD in eligible Binance accounts. Eligible incremental holdings may qualify for up to a 1.3× reward multiplier. APRs are updated weekly. More here → https://t.co/CYCSS51Yrv https://t.co/a1IyTWSWHl.

Eligible customers must hold RLUSD in their balances (net assets) in either their Binance Spot Accounts, Funding Accounts, and Earn Accounts (RLUSD in Flexible Savings) or their Margin Accounts (RLUSD in Cross Margin, Isolated Margin, or Portfolio Margin). Eligible users must maintain at least 0.01 RLUSD in their Spot, Funding, Earn, or Margin Accounts to qualify for the rewards.

Rewards will be airdropped directly to the Spot Accounts of eligible people’ Binance master accounts and will start accruing on November 20, 2026, at 00:00 (UTC). Weekly rewards will be distributed by 18:00 (UTC) every Friday in XRP.

This continues Binance’s recent streak of rewarding RLUSD holders with XRP giveaways in recent months.

In a recent development, meanwhile, RLUSD continues to gain traction. Ripple's dollar-pegged stablecoin now ranks as the sixth-largest stablecoin by circulating supply globally.

Currently, RLUSD has a market valuation of $2.8 billion; $746 million of this sits on the XRPL while the stablecoin continues to find newly introduced use cases on the blockchain.

According to recent reports, an AI agent pays on the XRP Ledger by requesting a service and gets a price back. It signs a payment in XRP or RLUSD. The service is delivered, and the XRPL x402 facilitator, provided by t54ai, verifies and settles the payment.

In separate news, Binance states it will extend the Monitoring Tag to include more tokens on November 20, 2026, based on recent reviews. The tokens to be added to the Monitoring Tag list are Lorenzo Protocol (BANK), Initia (INIT), Mitosis (MITO), Harmony (ONE), THENA (THE), Zilliqa (ZIL). The tokens to be removed from the Seed Tag list are: Morpho Token (MORPHO), Hyperliquid (HYPE).

As of Nov. 20, Shiba Inu (SHIB) is about $10 million in market capitalization short of overtaking Bittensor (TAO) for the No. 33 spot in CoinMarketCap's global crypto ranking. TAO has a market cap of $2.18 billion at a price of $186.41, and SHIB has $2.17 billion at $0.000003691 and ranks No. 34.

A gain of about 0.5% in SHIB's price, with TAO's price unchanged, would be enough for the meme coin to take Bittensor's place in the ranking.

TAO is the token of the Bittensor AI network, and Digital Currency Group (DCG) founder Barry Silbert has been one of its most vocal backers. Silbert also runs Yuma, a DCG manufacturer that builds on Bittensor.

Recent findings suggest that at Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference in September 2025, Silbert remarked that Bittensor was the thing he had gotten most excited about since Bitcoin. "I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence.".

On Dec. 30, 2025, DCG's Grayscale filed with the SEC to convert its Grayscale Bittensor Trust into a spot exchange-traded fund on NYSE Arca under the ticker GTAO. The filing came after Bittensor's first halving in mid-December 2025, and at the end of that month, TAO was trading at about $222. "We're pleased to take this early step as we continue to expand the tools available to investors," a Grayscale spokesperson remarked.

Recent findings suggest that the gap between the two tokens closed because TAO fell. TAO was one of the market's strongest tokens this year. In April, the token was up 55% since January, and in October it rallied again and was up 43% for the year, according to TradingView data.

The November correction erased those gains. On Nov. 20, TAO was trading 16.95% below its January level, and it lost 12.16% over the past week.

SHIB spent most of the year in the red. The meme coin rose about 25% in January, and it has not been in positive territory since February. By Nov. 20, SHIB had lost about 50% since the start of the year, and it fell 13.79% over the past week.

TAO had a 24-hour trading volume of $172.19 million on Nov. 20, and SHIB had $55.17 million, according to CoinMarketCap data. TAO has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens, the same as Bitcoin's, and SHIB has about 589 trillion tokens in circulation.

Sources indicate that shiba Inu developer Mazrael responded to the drop on X on Nov. 17. "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB," he wrote in reply to a user who pointed to the falling price.

#41644. Tech Report: There’s a Ton of Conspiracies About Lab-Grown Meat Right Now. Here’s What’s Really True.
