General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: There’s a Ton of Conspiracies About Lab-Grown Meat Right Now. Here’s What’s Really True.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1240 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lab-grown meat is having an absolute field day on social media, as tons of outlandish claims and conspiracy theories about it are forming: The lab-grown industry is trying to sneak it into our grocery carts by labeling it as natural meat!
  • According to recent reports, formally known as cultivated meat, lab-grown meat has been in development for more than a decade, but it’s only recently begun to capture mainstream attention.
  • Meet the experts: Elliot Swartz, PhD, is a cultivated meat researcher and the senior principal scientist for cultivated meat at The Good Food Institute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lab-grown meat is having an absolute field day on social media, as tons of outlandish claims and conspiracy theories about it are forming: The lab-grown industry is trying to sneak it into our grocery carts by labeling it as natural meat! Here’s why you need to avoid it at all costs! In truth, there’s a lot more to the story, and a ton of those claims are false.

According to recent reports, formally known as cultivated meat, lab-grown meat has been in development for more than a decade, but it’s only recently begun to capture mainstream attention. In 2023, it received regulatory clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). Now, it’s beginning to make its way into the market (albeit in limited quantities), says Steven Surico, RD, a registered dietitian with the Food and Nutrition Department at Good Samaritan University Hospital.

Meet the experts: Elliot Swartz, PhD, is a cultivated meat researcher and the senior principal scientist for cultivated meat at The Good Food Institute. Steven Surico, RD, is a registered dietitian with the Food and Nutrition Department at Good Samaritan University Hospital. Lauri Wright, RDN, is a registered dietitian and associate professor of nutrition and dietetics at the University of South Florida College of Public Health.

As such, lab-grown meat is becoming a grossly misunderstood concept. (Cue: The recent influx of misleading social media videos and AI-generated content.) These posts can blur the line between fact and fiction, leaving consumers unsure of what’s real, scaring them when there’s nothing to be afraid of. “The concern is that cultivated meat is something highly artificial, when in reality, it’s not,” indicates Surico.

Here’s everything you need to know about lab-grown meat, including what it is, whether it’s being sold in stores, and if you should truly worry about it, according to experts.

Cultivated meat is grown directly from animal cells, as opposed to natural meat that’s produced by raising and slaughtering an animal, claims Elliot Swartz, PhD, a cultivated meat researcher and the senior principal scientist for cultivated meat at The Good Food Institute.

Industry observers note that “A small sample of cells is fed basic nutrients, like amino acids, fats, vitamins, salts, and sugars, in clean, controlled environments similar to those used to make yogurt, cheese, and beer, where the cells are grown and developed into meat or seafood,” he explains. As the cells multiply and develop, they form the muscle and other tissues that make up meat. Once mature, Swartz indicates they’re harvested and prepared as a product that should, at least in theory, offer the same taste, smell, texture, and consistency as ordinary meat.

Lab-grown meat vs. plant-based alternatives: “Beyond Meat products are made primarily from plant ingredients and do not contain animal muscle cells, whereas cultivated meat starts with animal cells and grows those cells into animal tissue,” Surico says.

It has been revealed that cultivated meat may address some of the challenges associated with natural meat production, particularly when it comes to food safety, public health, nutrition, and the environmental impact of raising livestock. According to Swartz, one of the biggest advantages is the greater control over the production process, which could offer significant food safety benefits.

Research shows that raising large populations of animals in close quarters can create opportunities for bacteria, other pathogens, and diseases to spread. This can increase the risk of transmission to humans through food (or animal) contact, but cultivated meat could help reduce these risks, Swartz explains.

Cultivated meat is also better for the environment by reducing the land, water, and greenhouse gas emissions needed for meat production. Research from The Good Food Institute even suggests that if cultivated meat can be produced commercially in large quantities using clean energy, it could have a significantly smaller environmental footprint than conventional meat.

Finally, because the cells are grown in a controlled environment, researchers can influence the nutritional composition of the meat, notes Lauri Wright, RDN, a registered dietitian and associate professor of nutrition and dietetics at the University of South Florida College of Public Health. For example, they can adjust the amount and types of fat in the meat to reduce saturated fat and cholesterol while increasing desirable nutrients like protein, she explains. Theoretically, this could lead to healthier meat that tastes the same, studies suggest.

While some people are afraid of lab-grown meat because they’re not really sure what’s in it, each product undergoes extensive testing by the FDA and USDA. So, its nutritional content is thoroughly tested to ensure it meets food safety standards, adds Swartz.

Yes, but availability is extremely limited. Cultivated meat has received approval from the FDA and USDA for sale in the U.S., as well as in Singapore and Australia, per The Good Food Institute. However, regulatory approval doesn’t necessarily mean that products are widely available. Plus, eight states in the U.S. have enacted bans or temporary restrictions on cultivated meat, including Alabama, Florida, Indiana, Mississippi, Montana, South Dakota, Nebraska, and Texas. These restrictions are largely driven by concerns about protecting traditional agriculture and livestock industries.

So, contrary to what social media might have you believing, cultivated meat isn’t something you can pick up at your local supermarket just yet. In the U.S., the only product currently being served is Wildtype’s cultivated salmon, which is available at a handful of select restaurants in Washington D.C., Oregon, Arizona, and California.

Sources indicate that while it’s difficult to predict exactly when lab-grown meat will be in grocery stores, Swartz expects a gradual rollout, with smaller, more specialized retailers being the first to carry it. “You could start to see cultivated meat products more widely introduced in higher-end retailers in the early 2030s, but I don’t think you’ll see it in significant box grocery stores until the late 2030s,” he states.

According to recent reports, in grocery stores, it’ll be clearly labeled as lab-grown or cultivated meat. “Due to the USDA regulations and labeling, it should be very clear to the consumer if they are buying regular meat or lab-grown meat,” states Surico. In fact, federal law prohibits food from being misbranded or carrying false or misleading labels, and regulators have said cultivated meat products must be clearly and accurately labeled.

According to recent reports, as for the price, that remains to be seen. Cultivated meat is currently more expensive to produce than most conventional meat and seafood, but Swartz says the long-term goal is to bring production costs down to match or fall below those of conventional options.

Not very. “You should not be freaked out,” states Wright. “If anything, you should see it as potential, because the future of lab-grown meat could give consumers more options and alternatives to what they buy and put into their body.”.

Recent findings suggest that swartz agrees, pointing out that the benefits go beyond offering another way to produce meat. “Whether you care about the environment, animal welfare, food safety, or public health, there’s a lot of potential benefits for cultivated meat that are additive in terms of value for the consumer,” he says.

Of course, that doesn’t mean everyone has to embrace cultivated meat—traditional meat isn’t going away or being phased out of grocery stores or restaurants. The goal is simply to give consumers another option, not replace the foods they already know and enjoy. And if cultivated meat isn’t your jam, that’s perfectly fine, too.

Significant long liquidations were seen for Zcash, accelerating its price decline as leveraged positions unwind, particularly with traders being heavily concentrated on the same side of the market.

At the time of writing, ZEC was down 14.53% in the last 24 hours, recording the heaviest losses in the top 20, while NEAR Protocol was down 13.03% in the same timeframe.

Industry observers note that zcash is entering its third day of a drop that began on November 18, even as the broader crypto market slid as the tech-stock selloff spread. The rapid unwind suggests a leverage shakeout amid volatility following Anthropic’s IPO.

Anthropic debuted on the Nasdaq on November 19, 2026, under the ticker symbol ANT, raising about $81.3 billion in the public offering (and $107.3 billion combined with a $26 billion private placement).

Over the last 24 hours, volume across crypto futures rose 29.31% to $250 billion, while open interest (OI) fell 3.07% to $109.29 billion, according to CoinGlass data. That combination suggests traders are unwinding positions, with net capital exiting the futures market.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the back of an iffy Q3, many were hoping Q4 would turn out to be better.
  • It has been revealed that both these altcoins are in the news today after Roundhill ETF Trust revealed that it will be ditching plans to launch two exchange-traded funds or ETFs tied to them.
  • The Trust no longer intends to seek effectiveness of the Fund.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the back of an iffy Q3, many were hoping Q4 would turn out to be better. Unfortunately, that hasn’t been the case. Especially for those in the XRP and Solana markets.

It has been revealed that both these altcoins are in the news today after Roundhill ETF Trust revealed that it will be ditching plans to launch two exchange-traded funds or ETFs tied to them. It cited no specific reason in its filings with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission for these new plans.

The Trust no longer intends to seek effectiveness of the Fund.

It went on to add that “… no securities of the Fund were sold, or will be sold.”.

The registration documents for both these ETFs were filed way back in October 2025. That’s over a year ago. As recently as 06 November, the Trust had submitted an extension. This would have allowed the registrations to become effective by 06 December.

However, an important distinction must be made here. It must be pointed out that the ETFs Roundhill was planning to launch were income-focused products. These ETFs would have relied on income generated by trading Options linked to existing crypto prodcuts.

Now, while more recent and fewer in number compared to funds that directly hold these tokens, these products have seen little interest lately.

Consider Amplify’s SOLM, for instance. At the time of writing, it held net assets worth just $1.36 million. This, despite being rolled out in November last year. Similarly, the fund manager’s XRPM had net assets worth just over $7.66 million in over a year since its launch.

Industry observers note that these numbers are pretty startling, especially when compared to and juxtaposed against the figures reported by other Solana or XRP-focused ETFs. According to SoSoValue, for instance, combined, both these ETF products attracted over $969 million from May to October 2026.

This, despite recent market weakness hitting these ETF products too. Less than 24 hours ago, XRP ETFs saw outflows of over $6 million, with the Canary XRP ETF (XRPC) and the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF (GXRP) particulalry affected. This, after the week ending ending 13th November saw outflows of $19.1 million. This was the largest single-week withdrawal in nearly eight months.

In a similar vein, the assets under management for Spot Solana ETFs fell from $1.79 billion on 25th September to $947 million on 18th November.

#41638. Michelle Yeoh on Strength, Stunts, and What Makes Us Human

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

Michelle Yeoh on Strength, Stunts, and What Makes Us Human

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2240 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that an action hero used to have to be substantial and brawny and brusque.
  • Starring as Olwen, a bioengineered artificial human (or “replicant,” as they’re called in the Blade Runner universe, which includes the fresh series Blade Runner 2099, out November 25 on Amazon Prime Video), the 64-year-old global megastar literally wrestles with people and replicants alike on-screen.
  • But in real life, she dances with even larger issues.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that an action hero used to have to be substantial and brawny and brusque. Michelle Yeoh is none of those things—but you feel her presence and power the instant you meet her. She is kind, warm, and lovely, but she’s also intense…in a really good way. This is a person who listens closely yet also seems ready to launch into a wheelhouse kick at any moment.

Starring as Olwen, a bioengineered artificial human (or “replicant,” as they’re called in the Blade Runner universe, which includes the fresh series Blade Runner 2099, out November 25 on Amazon Prime Video), the 64-year-old global megastar literally wrestles with people and replicants alike on-screen.

But in real life, she dances with even larger issues. Like what separates humans from the bot world, how we define strength beyond the physical, why we all need to stretch every morning, and, finally, how she gets over a very specific fear. (If you’ve ever watched her in movies like Tomorrow Never Dies or even Everything Everywhere All At Once, you’ll understand how shocking this particular fear is for her. The solution is one six-letter word…and you’ll just have to read on to find out what that is.).

I sat down with Michelle—who is classically trained in ballet and does many of her own martial arts stunts—in NYC for a wide-ranging convo that starts with robots and ends with what she calls the “Michelle prayer.”.

Women’s Health: What was it like to play a replicant, and how did you think about preparing and training for that mindset?

It has been revealed that michelle Yeoh: We have a brilliant writer, Silka Luisa, who had thought out the story for Blade Runner 2099 [a continuation of the original series] and where it has gone. All these replicants are now in charge of a Los Angeles that is no longer what we know. But it’s very interesting because [the question that arises is] What is humanity? The replicants do give the humans hope. As long as you’re good, as long as you do things the way we want them to be handled, you could go to a better place, because now Los Angeles is not exactly the most habitable place.

Sources indicate that replicants are made to look human. In fact, they are flesh and blood, except they’re stronger, faster. They are able to withstand the newly introduced worlds. But empathy is what gives you away as a human. Replicants are born without that emotion. They’re born with memories. They’re given memories to keep them sort of happy and at peace with what they are. Are you born with humanity or does it come with experience and as you live your life with compassion and kindness?

In a recent development, WH: You stated that you’re excited for people to see the series and to share ideas and to talk about it. Is that why? The humanity complexity?

Recent findings suggest that michelle: The worst is they say, “Oh, yeah, it was interesting.…” What is “just” interesting? Hopefully you go home, you think about it, and then you come back and the next day at work or in school, you’re chatting with your friends— “Well, what are you? A replicant or a human? What would you rather be?”.

WH: How did you prepare, physically, for this role?

Michelle: I think the older you get, the more you have to do to keep up your muscle strength, to keep your muscles there. Without that, you start walking differently. I have the advantage of understanding my body a lot more because I’ve been doing this for the last, well, ever since I was born. I was dancing, doing sports, everything. I do core-strengthening exercises and tai chi every day.

According to recent reports, the core was the most important part of the training because we wanted to nail the way Olwen moved. It was with precision. Because if you want to move with motivation, it has to have that strength, that inner strength, rather than just speed. So when you move, it’s almost like you glide. As a replicant, all the moves are sharp, precise, because they’re so strong and powerful. Actually, when you take a human down, it’s too easy. I think all exercises are core-focused. You can’t lift weights or do pilates without working on the core first. Everything has to start from there.

Sources indicate that WH: Has your own relationship to risk changed over the years? Are there stunts that you used to do in your 30s that now you’re like “nah,” or do you actually feel more powerful and in control?

Michelle: I think that’s really interesting and a good way of putting it. Feeling powerful doesn’t mean being reckless and silly. I feel more powerful in the sense that I have a better assessment of the risk factors. But naturally, because when I was in my 20s, when I first started out, you’re brave and foolish and you’re also so fit. And I was really, really, really fit at that time because I didn’t have any crazy injuries. And, so, fearless is a good word, but fearless and stupid is not good. That’s a bad combination.

In a recent development, sometimes the smallest stunts are the worst because you think they’re easy, and then you don’t pay full attention. You’re not focused enough. You’re focused, but you’re like, “Yeah, yeah, yeah. I’ll get it done.” And that’s when something bad will happen.

In the past, when you are beginning, you listen and you do what they tell you to do, and then you have a lot to prove because you don’t want them to think that you’re unable or you’re not capable, so you do it. But now you go, “How about we…” And then you can speak with power because you know your character. And then I’ll go, “But Olwen won’t do it like that.” And who is going to challenge me?

Industry observers note that WH: I understand that you became a bit of a mentor to Hunter Schafer. So talk to us a little about the stunt piece.… Did you help her figure out how to have that voice for herself?

Michelle: To be honest, when I look at her, I go, “Oh my god, I see my young self.” When they show her something, she’ll just throw herself into it because she wants to do it. She’s eager to do it. But then I have to keep reminding her, “You don’t have the same kind of training the stunt people have. So when you can’t do it, it doesn’t mean that you’re not good.”.

In a recent development, what I do is try to remind her, like, “Hunter, knee pads, Hunter, elbow pads. What is the stunt that you’re doing? Get them on.” Because sometimes you go, like, No, no, no, it’s okay. It’s not okay. Get it on.

It’s a joy to work with her. It’s just a joy to be with her, which sometimes can be difficult because we’re supposed to be against each other in Blade Runner 2099. I mean, she’s a human pretending to be a replicant, pretending to be a blade runner. But somehow their missions intertwine, so they have no choice but to learn to work together. So we have a lot of fun.

WH: What are your nonnegotiables? What are the things you, Michelle, must do every single day for your health that you are consistent with?

Michelle: Water, sunblock, and a lot of stretching. That is a must.

In a recent development, I do tai chi, I do my ballet and tai chi. I’ve been doing that for a long time now. I try to do that every day because I’ve unfortunately had injuries in the past—my back, my knees, my shoulder. I don’t know where I don’t have an injury. As I’m in bed, I do a lot of stretching. When I wake up, the first thing I do in my bed is to go through the motions so that the body wakes up with the mind and everything comes into place.

Industry observers note that I think that’s what you have to find: your own moves [or routine] so that you don’t give yourself an excuse when you go, “Oh, it’s raining. No time to go to the gym.” So you just do it even in the bed, you’re stretching, you’re doing all those core exercises to wake up the mind, to wake up the abs, the back, and the legs, everything. And that helps when we’re actually on-set because then I can step into it and know I am strong and ready to go.

In a recent development, I love being outside, going on hikes. Then if I can’t do that, I’m on the elliptical, because I think cardio is still very notable. But now, with time, I do a lot more weights. I’m picking up dumbbells or water bottles, whatever works. You have to combine the strengthening of muscles with cardio exercise.

WH: I’m curious if there’s something that is better now in your 60s than it was in your 20s—anything?

Michelle: I think the only thing that’s a little bit better might be this up here [motions to head].

I do a fairly decent job at keeping up the energy, keeping up the spirits, because I also think it’s the inner strength that is very important. Your mind is very important. If you don’t have the inner peace, it’s very hard to keep control of your body because negative vibes are the worst thing for any human being. When you have negative vibes around you, in you, then you’re down. I honestly believe that because you’ve gone through so many experiences, you’re better for it. I wouldn’t give that up.

Michelle: I have a fear of heights. I know. See, I’m claustrophobic and have a fear of heights.

Recent findings suggest that michelle: But the magic word is action. Camera rolling…action. And I am focused. Fearless. It’s really, really bizarre. If I don’t hear the word action, then it’s a no go. If I’m in the mall, you know, sometimes you have those walkways that look over the first floor. I walk right in the middle of those. I’m taking no risk. But once action is remarked on set, I’m good.

WH: You mentioned a mantra. What, exactly, is it?

According to recent reports, michelle: When I wake up, even before opening my eyes and stretching, I sort of have my own little mantra to wake myself up. I try to talk to my body, thank my body, apologize for anything I’ve done bad, and then welcome everything that’s good because I’m deserving of it.

I don’t sit there and meditate. I don’t understand that at all. Just as long as you feel it yourself that I have what I need for me…because everybody is different.

And that’s why I start my day with a prayer, a mantra. I guess you could call it my own Michelle prayer. Be thankful and be willing to accept anything good that comes your way. I think we have to look at ourselves and have self-worth because I think the inner strength, the inner peace, that sense of compassion and kindness and contentment, is very crucial. Because if you’re always wanting, needing, and thinking about something else, someone else, then you’re always in conflict, first of all, with yourself.

WH: What does the word strength mean to you? When you hear that word, what’s the definition that comes to mind?

According to recent reports, michelle: I think when you hear that word, first of all, it’s always very top layer. You walk into the gym, I have strength, I have power. I put on a power suit. That’s powerful. But for me, true strength is right in there [points to heart]. Showing weakness is strength. Doing a lot of things that people don’t understand, but for you, when you make a choice, it’s strength. There are so many ways of looking at it, and I don’t think there’s one definition unless you check the encyclopedia and they tell you what it is.

WH: And then we’ll just ignore that and go with the Michelle Yeoh definition anyway.

*This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity*.

Abigail has almost 20 years of editing and writing experience at national publications, with a specific expertise in health and medical journalism. She’s edited award-winning features and packages and is passionate about creating impactful stories that engage and inform the audience. Abigail hails from the Midwest (Urbana, Illinois) and is a proud alum of Syracuse University, graduating with a specialty focus in exercise physiology in addition to magazine journalism. She’s completed 6 marathons, countless half-marathons, and 1 half-ironman. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • What started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million users worldwide.
  • Industry observers note that the scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients.
  • Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into new industries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million users worldwide. As WhiteBIT celebrates its eighth anniversary and W Group marks its first year, the milestones highlight a transformation from a single trading platform into a diversified business connecting traditional finance, digital assets, and emerging technologies.

Industry observers note that the scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients. Meanwhile, W Group has expanded from eight to 11 companies in one year, growing its combined user base from 35 million to approximately 40 million.

Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into new industries.

The group aims to build more than a portfolio of independent companies. By combining financial infrastructure, technology and expertise, its businesses can develop new services, reach new markets and create opportunities across industries.

In 2026, W Group expanded well beyond financial services. Dutch sports car manufacturer Spyker joined the group in June, opening opportunities to apply digital finance and blockchain technology to luxury automotive.

W Group has also made a $400 million investment commitment in SignSplit, the signed-data platform for the AI era. The seed round values SignSplit at $1 billion.

In banking, Georgia-based hashbank, a fully licensed digital bank, combines traditional banking services with cryptocurrency functionality, allowing customers to manage fiat and digital assets within one environment.

Together, these businesses illustrate W Group’s strategy of connecting financial services, technology, and consumer-facing products into an ecosystem where each organization can contribute to the growth of the others.

WhiteBIT remains a central pillar of W Group, providing trading infrastructure and digital asset services for retail and institutional clients.

In a recent development, in 2026, the exchange recorded $2.8 trillion in trading volume, with derivatives generating approximately $3.5 billion in daily activity. Its platform now offers nearly 1,200 trading markets.

Trading conditions have also improved. Spot trading volume across WhiteBIT’s flagship BTC, ETH and WBT pairs increased more than fivefold, from $53 billion in 2020 to $276 billion in 2025. Meanwhile, bid-ask spreads across its major markets have narrowed approximately threefold since 2021, reflecting deeper liquidity.

WhiteBIT also serves more than 5,500 institutional clients, including funds, brokers and payment providers, through over 20 dedicated products and services. Businesses can access crypto liquidity, manage digital asset transactions and move between fiat currencies and cryptocurrencies through a single platform.

WhiteBIT’s eighth year brought significant regulatory milestones that strengthen the group’s international presence.

In June 2026, WhiteBIT EU secured authorisation under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) from Austria’s Financial Market Authority, establishing a regulatory foundation for providing crypto-asset services across the European Union.

In May, WhiteBIT released a dedicated platform for users in the United Kingdom, expanding into another major financial market with demanding regulatory requirements. The company also joined Ghana’s regulatory sandbox in March, contributing to the development of the country’s digital asset regulatory framework.

These developments reflect WhiteBIT’s investment in compliance as a foundation for sustainable international growth.

The growth of the ecosystem is also reflected in WBT, WhiteBIT’s native coin, which reached an all-time high of nearly $88 in September 2026, up from its launch price of $1.62 in 2022.*The milestone reflects WBT’s strong long-term performance alongside the expansion of WhiteBIT and its ecosystem.

It has been revealed that WBT’s role is also expanding beyond trading. In November, Whitechain transitioned into an Ethereum Layer 2 network built on the OP Stack in partnership with Optimism, with WBT used to pay transaction fees. Designed to support blockchain applications and financial services, Whitechain has already attracted interest from developers, with more than 140 teams applying to its Builders Program ahead of the network’s public launch planned for later in November.

For W Group, the next stage of growth will focus on connecting its businesses more closely and turning their combined capabilities into latest products and services.

Recent findings suggest that “Eight years ago, we started with one cryptocurrency exchange. Today, we’ve grown into an international group of 11 companies serving around 40 million users. But our ambition has never been simply to build more businesses. We want to connect them in ways that create real value — bringing traditional finance and digital assets closer together, making newly introduced technologies more accessible and opening opportunities across industries,” remarked Volodymyr Nosov, Founder and President of W Group.

Looking ahead, W Group aims to strengthen its presence in regulated markets, expand institutional financial services and accelerate blockchain infrastructure development. Its long-term vision is an interconnected ecosystem where banking, payments, digital assets and emerging technologies work together, making financial services more accessible to people and businesses worldwide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility. However, recent onchain data has shown an unexpected trend in exchange activity.

According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is currently facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.

According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.

Notably, the data further highlights that the metric has surpassed the previous reading of 2.09 recorded on July 6, marking a five-month high in XRP’s supply shortage index.

It is important to note that readings above +2 are a strong indication of severely tightened supply, which means that the amount of XRP available on the exchange has decreased significantly.

While negative readings often mean the opposite, this means that XRP has witnessed a sharp reversal from the supply level seen on September 27.

At the time, the index stood at -1.5 while XRP traded above $1.50, signaling an abundance of XRP on Binance. This means that more tokens were available for trading during the period, which potentially added to selling pressure.

While that is no longer the case, the latest data highlights that the XRP supply index has jumped by 3.9 points in just 53 days, moving from supply abundance to severe supply tightness in just about two months.

This typically suggests that XRP is being aggressively moved out of exchanges despite its prolonged price weakness, potentially driving a rebound in the demand for XRP, which could eventually trigger a price recovery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Cardano [ADA] Treasury Foundation wants 25 million ADA to host 12 events in 2027. Its last $22 million proposal (to buy copper) barely got any votes at all.

Hence, the question — Will this one fare any better?

On 16th November, the Cardano Foundation filed a proposal to pull 24,995,775 ADA from the network’s treasury. The money would pay for Cardano’s presence at 12 crypto events next year.

Some of the biggest names on the circuit are on the list. Consensus in Miami, TOKEN2049 in both Singapore and New York, Web Summit in Lisbon, and India Blockchain Week in Bangalore.

The run kicks off in February with the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi.

$2 million will go towards sponsorships and $1.06 million for booths and equipment. Travel is said to cost $702K, while side events will account for $695,000.

According to the Foundation, none of it covers salaries or profit. Whatever isn’t spent goes back to the treasury.

However, here’s what’s tricky. The Foundation priced ADA at $0.20 to reach its $5 million budget. ADA, however, was valued at $0.15 at press time. At that price, the request is worth about $3.85 million. That is a gap of over $1 million.

For the budget to work as planned, ADA needs to climb by almost 30%. Not impossible, but far from guaranteed.

DReps, the delegates who vote on treasury spending, have until 20th December to decide.

Will 25 million ADA move the price? Probably not. There are about 37.6 billion ADA in circulation. So, this withdrawal will merely be a drop in the ocean.

However, it’s worth pointing out that the chart had bigger problems at press time.

ADA fell from $0.25 in October to $0.155 following a price drop on the 14th.

Is a pause imminent? We might be in the early stages, yes. The RSI fell to 21 after that drop, with the same since climbing to 32, just crossing above its average. The OI has also recovered from about $145 million to $153.5 million. Finally, the funding rates were positive yesterday.

On the contrary, the Chaikin Money Flow was negative, implying that sellers might still have a slight edge.

#41629. Can You Lose 10 Pounds In A Month? Experts Share 15 Tips For Safe Weight Loss In 30 Days

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1749 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

Can You Lose 10 Pounds In A Month? Experts Share 15 Tips For Safe Weight Loss In 30 Days

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It only makes sense to want to give your weight loss journey everything you’ve got.
  • Here's the truth: The average person cannot safely lose 10 pounds in a month, says Michael Glickman, MD, a board-certified family medicine and obesity medicine physician and founder of Revolution Medicine, Health and Fitness.
  • According to recent reports, meet the experts: Michael Glickman, MD, is a board-certified family medicine and obesity medicine physician and founder of Revolution Medicine, Health and Fitness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It only makes sense to want to give your weight loss journey everything you’ve got. And, if you’re into big goals, you may wonder if it’s safe to lose 10 pounds in a month.

Here's the truth: The average person cannot safely lose 10 pounds in a month, says Michael Glickman, MD, a board-certified family medicine and obesity medicine physician and founder of Revolution Medicine, Health and Fitness. Losing weight at this aggressive of a pace can raise your risk of developing gallstones (painful deposits of digestive fluid in the gallbladder) and up the odds that you’ll regain the weight down the line, he says. (Neither of those are ideal!).

According to recent reports, meet the experts: Michael Glickman, MD, is a board-certified family medicine and obesity medicine physician and founder of Revolution Medicine, Health and Fitness. Michael Hamlin, CSCS, is a certified strength and conditioning specialist and the founder of Everflex Fitness.

According to recent reports, of course, everyone is different and a lot depends on your starting weight. Also, you can still have aggressive goals when it comes to weight loss—it’s just that 10 pounds in a too-short timeframe is a tricky benchmark for most people. So, how much weight can you safely lose in a month—and how should you even go about it? Here’s what experts suggest.

The timeline will be different for everyone, given factors like starting weight, genetics, nutrition, activity level, stress, and more. But Dr. Glickman says to give yourself anywhere from two to three months to hit that 10-pounds-lost goal. “For some, this could take longer, so be compassionate with your body and prioritize what’s best for your health,” he says.

Sources indicate that when it comes to how much weight is safe to lose at a given time, stick to one to two pounds per week, notes Dr. Glickman. “Some people can shed weight more quickly in the first month after instituting a lower calorie and healthy diet, however much of the weight loss on the scale will have been due to water weight.”.

If you have obesity and are revamping your eating habits, along with starting an exercise program after being fairly sedentary, you may see bigger gains early on than someone with a lower starting weight who isn’t making drastic changes.

First things first: A safe way to lose weight is a holistic and multi-factorial approach that involves optimal nutrition, frequent exercise, stress reduction, and adequate sleep, says Dr. Glickman. It's not necessarily about eating less but being conscious of the diversity of plants in your diet, and the avoidance of processed foods, refined oils, and refined carbohydrates, he explains.

On top of that, apply sustainable healthy changes to your routine that you enjoy, says Michael Hamlin, CSCS, a certified strength and conditioning specialist and the founder of Everflex Fitness. Maybe that means attending a workout class with friends twice a week, cooking a plant-based dinner with your partner, or throwing on your favorite podcast and going for a solo walk.

Sleep deprivation promotes an increase in ghrelin, your hunger hormone, which can trigger late night snacking, ultimately increasing your daily caloric intake, claims Dr. Glickman. So do your best to get seven to nine hours of sleep per night. Not only that, getting more sleep helps you feel more energized, so you can add more activity to your day.

It has been revealed that it may sound simple, but 30 minutes of daily walking can do wonders, states Dr. Glickman. “It isn’t about calorie burning—it’s about the mobility, the happy hormones your brain releases, and the physiological anti-inflammatory responses that have long-term impacts on your weight.”.

Getting daily steps in has health benefits ranging from lowering your risk of developing type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease to helping you live longer. While any movement is good, moving at a brisk pace is the best way to get in all those extra perks.

Plant diversity has been shown to have the most beneficial impact on the gut microbiome, which influences your metabolic set point (the body’s preferred weight), insulin levels, and fat storage, indicates Dr. Glickman. Plant-based diets are also linked to a lower risk of developing heart disease, stroke, and diabetes, making this a significant win for your overall health, too.

In a recent development, his suggestion? Try a plant-based day or meal per week to ensure you’re supporting your gut microbiome and loading up on the veggies.

It’s best to consult a doctor or registered dietitian to determine your daily caloric needs since it depends on your age, gender, activity level, muscle mass, current weight, and the amount of calories you burn at rest (a.k.a. your basal metabolic rate), indicates Hamlin. From there, they can determine a slight calorie deficit, or how many calories you need in a day to lose one to two pounds a week, he explains.

While you’re waiting for a consult, check out the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases’ online body weight planner. It asks you to enter some basic information like your current weight, your ideal weight, and your activity level, and provides what your daily calorie goals should be to help you get there.

According to recent reports, “Stress can lead to increased hunger hormones and an elevated metabolic set point,” indicates Dr. Glickman. Higher levels of the stress hormone cortisol can create stubborn fat distribution around the abdomen, he adds.

Although this one is often easier mentioned than done, to help combat stress and anxiety, try relaxation techniques like meditation, yoga, and journaling. And, of course, if you’re struggling with stress management, consider reaching out to a mental health therapist for individual guidance on navigating everything.

“Sometimes we can mistake the feeling of thirst for hunger, so make sure to stay hydrated throughout the day, especially during and after exercise,” Dr. Glickman states. Women should drink about 11.5 cups (2.7 liters) of fluids a day, per Mayo Clinic. (Note: That total can come from food and liquids.).

Recent findings suggest that strength training has a significant impact on your metabolism and fat burning capabilities, studies show, so incorporate resistance training at least three days a week, indicates Dr. Glickman. Just take note that because strength training builds muscle, you may notice little or even no overall weight change at times, even though you are losing fat. (Not sure where to start with your strength training journey? Try Women's Health's The Woman's Guide To Strength Training: Dumbbells.).

According to recent reports, HIIT workouts burn a ton of calories and can change your body composition while building muscle, notes Hamlin. In fact, women who incorporated HIIT programming achieved similar body composition and aerobic capacity results in half the time as women who did moderate-intensity workouts, a 2017 study published in the Journal of Diabetes Research found.

Industry observers note that fiber helps regulate blood sugar levels, prevent insulin resistance and diabetes, and is an excellent source of nutrition for healthy bacteria in the gut, says Dr. Glickman. High-fiber foods like vegetables are also filling without overloading on the calories, explains Hamlin. You can get fiber in powder or supplement form, but your best (and healthiest) bet is from plants, adds Dr. Glickman.

It has been revealed that weight gain is linked with the consumption of highly processed and packaged foods, Dr. Glickman notes. “This includes any food item in a wrapper with ingredients you can’t pronounce, even if the calories and carbohydrates seem appealing,” he explains. “Always choose whole foods over packaged ones.”.

Do your best to prioritize cooking at home to eliminate sneaky fats, sugars, and processed ingredients that are not listed on a menu, says Dr. Glickman.

In a recent development, focus on the quality of food on your plate and aim for three hearty meals a day that include a small amount of complex carbohydrates (root veggies and whole grains), a moderate amount of high-quality protein (fish, chicken, eggs, and tofu), and lots of plant-based fiber, claims Dr. Glickman.

According to recent reports, alcoholic drinks lack nutritional value and are usually packed with calories, so it’s best to scale back on booze, states Hamlin. When you drink alcohol, it also immediately goes to the liver where it’s prioritized as an energy source, so your body burns alcohol cals first. Not only that, alcohol also lowers your inhibitions and raises the odds you’ll eat more than you need to feel satiated.

It has been revealed that to help with accountability, Hamlin suggests using a food journal or app to track your meals. This will give you a better understanding and awareness of how many calories you’re consuming and at which meal. Research demonstrates this is an effective way to lose weight, too. One study found that people who tracked their meals at least five days of each week had “significant and sustained weight loss” over time compared to people who tracked less or inconsistently.

It can take time for your stomach to recognize when it’s full, so pause in between portions before deciding if you actually want more, indicates Hamlin. You can either pre-pack your meals with smaller portion sizes or use smaller plates to provide a visual cue. One scientific analysis of 14 studies found that people who ate smaller portions had a “substantial” drop in how many calories they ate each day.

According to recent reports, think long-term about weight loss and establish a goal that is realistic for your lifestyle, says Hamlin. Your goals might take time and patience, but that’s okay, he adds. “Weight loss isn't solely about a caloric deficit, because the body is a super complex piece of machinery, and we can't simply boil all of weight loss down to calories in versus calories out.”.

Shiba Inu’s layer-2 network, Shibarium, is experiencing a major slowdown as daily network activity has fallen to three-digit figures (fewer than 1,000 transactions), hitting lows not seen in months.

Shibarium processed 546 transactions, according to Shibariumscan data, marking a slower period for the layer-2 network after activity spiked to a high of 6,370 on October 31, 2026. Transaction activity declined afterward, and the decline intensified amid the sell-off that hit the market in recent weeks.

Sources indicate that the latest figures suggest that fewer transactions are taking place across Shibarium compared with periods of stronger activity. The key question now is whether Shibarium can regain momentum in the coming weeks.

Meanwhile, development continues behind the scenes for the Shiba Inu layer-2 network, as long-time Shiba Inu community member and developer Mazrael revealed a massive batch of contracts deployed on Puppynet, Shibarium's testnet.

But in the meantime, Shibarium’s fall to three-digit activity levels is a major slowdown that SHIB holders and ecosystem watchers will be watching closely.

Shiba Inu's on-chain holders increased as the number of wallets holding SHIB hit 1,700,930 on November 19, 2026.

According to the latest figures shared by Etherscan SHIB, an X account dedicated to providing updates on the SHIB ecosystem, the cryptocurrency added 236 new on-chain holders in a single day, taking its total past the 1.7 million milestone.

The month of November has also seen consistent growth, with SHIB adding 4,520 holders since the start of the month. The broader 2026 trend is even more pronounced, with the number of holders of the token increasing by 152,300 since the beginning of the year.

While Shiba Inu's latest milestone seems remarkable, Mazrael suggested that the Shib ecosystem, including Shibarium, might have more holders than indicated, with 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on the BNB Chain.

According to recent reports, "Shibarium has more holders than those you listed, though. But yeah. Well, there are also 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on BNB. But that's not actually CCIP SHIB; it is a peg," Mazrael wrote.

A Fantastical Perch Above Toulon’s Old Port, Where Mermaids Meet Mediterranean Light

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that though perhaps not well known outside France, Vincent Darré is one of Paris’s most familiar figures—always on the scene, day and night.
  • Industry observers note that from his early days in fashion, which included stints at Moschino and Ungaro and a close, yearslong collaboration with none other than Karl Lagerfeld, Darré has followed a singular path, turning his creative energies to furniture and interiors with the opening of his own studio, Maison Darré, in 2008.
  • Sources indicate that in the formal salon, a pair of carved wood armchairs with inlaid stone backs have seat cushions of a Dedar fabric.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that though perhaps not well known outside France, Vincent Darré is one of Paris’s most familiar figures—always on the scene, day and night. The impish designer rarely just enters a room; he bounces in, impeccably dressed, with an infectious laugh and beautiful manners. At home in the worlds of fashion, society, art, and design, he is welcome at every table, always ready with a clever remark, a kind word, and no shortage of creative energy.

Industry observers note that from his early days in fashion, which included stints at Moschino and Ungaro and a close, yearslong collaboration with none other than Karl Lagerfeld, Darré has followed a singular path, turning his creative energies to furniture and interiors with the opening of his own studio, Maison Darré, in 2008. A pair of recently completed Paris hotels—L’Aventure, at the foot of the Arc de Triomphe, and Hôtel Le Magnifique, in the heart of Montparnasse—are propelling him onto the design scene in a bigger way than ever. His work has long encompassed scenography and ephemeral installations, among them crowd-pleasing turns at AD Intérieurs, the erstwhile annual showcase hosted by AD France.

Sources indicate that in the formal salon, a pair of carved wood armchairs with inlaid stone backs have seat cushions of a Dedar fabric. Darré-designed objects include his Calder table, Minos rug, and Lyre mirror. He also created the trompe-l’oeil pilasters topped with 18th-century gilded wooden capitals. Late-19th-century French lantern; 1940s Italian ceramic dolphin table.

According to recent reports, in the guest bedroom, Darré sits on an 18th-century gilded wood bench upholstered in velvet by Métaphores. A Darré-painted mural frames the 18th century Italian headboard upholstered in Tony Duquette’s Xanadu fabric for Jim Thompson. The bedcover and cushions are from Darré’s collection for Monoprix.

Darré was born in Paris, in the 14th, and went to school there as a boy. When his parents separated in the 1970s, his father—a sociologist—moved to the Luberon, and Vincent went with him; not long after, his mother, unwilling to live far from her son, also moved south, to Montpellier. “This allowed me to be Parisian, but also one who knew other places,” he says. It’s a telling detail: the South of France has informed his eye ever since, with its particular sense of light, water, and ease. Though he first went to school for fashion, his real love was drawing, as it had been since childhood. “Sometimes people are surprised,” he notes, “that a finished work of mine is almost always exactly like I had drawn it.”.

It has been revealed that after a series of Paris apartments over the years, Darré has recently acquired a getaway in Toulon, the Mediterranean port city. The attraction was immediate. He had been invited to preside over the jury of Design Parade, the summer design festival held in Toulon and Hyères, and the city seized him the moment he arrived. “Once I got to the airport, in 2017, I immediately felt I was home. Chez moi! I had never experienced that feeling before.” He kept an eye on the listings and, after a few false starts, found exactly what he wanted.

In the entrance, Darré’s Vase Soleil stands atop a 1940s Venetian console table against a wall decorated with trompe l’oeil caryatids.

A 19th-century rattan sofa upholstered in Jean Lurçat’s Sirenes fabric by Pierre Frey.

Overlooking the Toulon harbor, the primary bedroom’s office area features several Darré designs including his Orphée sconce, Singez-moi table lamp, the carved and lacquered wood desk, a Vertebré chair cushioned in a fabric by Pierre Le-Tan, and a Column stool.

In a recent development, lion head mascarons flank the doorway into the primary bedroom. 1970s plaster Buddha lamps with Darré-painted shades stand atop 17th-century French consoles. A 1960s plaster seahorse is displayed in the fireplace.

Recent findings suggest that the apartment occupies the top floor of a little three-story house overlooking the fishing port—a compact 860 square feet with stunning views of the sea. It was already lovely when he moved in, all white, with nothing architectural to be done: the perfect backdrop for Darré and his pencils and paints. He brought many of his favorite things—collections, objects, and furniture gathered over the years, added to since at the Drouot auction house and the little brocantes he loves to haunt. Furnishing was, he says, a gradual process, bringing in pieces little by little and slowly making the space his own over time.

Darré’s Crocodile bench stands in the primary bedroom. Two-Faced lamps with hand-painted shades atop Pas Gigogne tables flank the bed, and his Poisson bookcase is at left. The plaster chandelier is by Mathieu Challières, and the plaster unicorns are from a set designed by Jean Cocteau.

A metal figure given to Darré by Ines de la Fressange stands next to his Singez-moi lamp on the office area desk.

Darré’s Tabou shelf in the primary bedroom.

The exterior of the harbor-front house.

Darré on his Column stool with a 19th-century gilt-wood mirror from a Paris flea market.

It has been revealed that darré speaks often of his love for Toulon, and of Jean Cocteau, who adored this coast and painted frescoes nearby. “I like the sweetness of life here,” he states. “Nothing has really changed since the 1950s. It’s the Provence of another era.” Every little square has its fountain; everyone is kind. It’s a military port, but its douceur de vie is what holds him.

The apartment represents Vincent Darré to a T: not an unadorned surface in sight, a home full of memories, tributes, and joy. “This has been one of my dreams, to have a house on the water,” he indicates. “My place in Paris is exactly the same, though not on the water. But both are little suspended palaces. I create my own follies.” From the painted columns flanking the windows—among his very first purchases, which have followed him from home to home—to the mermaids and sea creatures and the tented bed, everything belongs to the fantastical world of Darré. As one of his teachers observed early on, you could recognize his hand from the very start.

A close-up of Darré’s ceramic Two-Faced lamp.

The dining area features a red lacquer table and chairs with Darré’s Dolphin lamp in the corner.

That world is entirely his own. He draws on a lineage of great fantasists—Charles de Beistegui, Henri Samuel, Jean Cocteau, Christian Bérard, Tony Duquette—yet the result, for all its jumble, is rigorously coherent. His flourish is always present. As the actress Isabelle Adjani once told him, to enter one of his interiors is to step into one of his drawings. Which is exactly what he wants.

According to recent reports, for all the bounce in his step, Darré is no one’s fool. He knows we live in difficult times, and likes the idea of adding a flourish of fantasy to reality. “I have my little world—a dream universe, but one you can live in.” He loves to dance, and even took tap-dancing lessons as a teenager, all the better to channel Fred Astaire or Gene Kelly. “Life is a film, and we are the actors,” he notes. “That’s why I always dress the way I do.” Lights, camera, action—Darré is always ready.

I Found the 11 Best Running Shoes for Women for Every Type of Run

📅 07 Dec 2023 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3759 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that LOW-IMPACT EXERCISES might be forever buzzy, but the running community is going stronger than ever.
  • As a former competitive runner who still throws down high mileage (50 to 60 miles weekly), I’ve learned the right footwear is crucial for allowing you to continue to pound the pavement, and selecting the right kind of running shoe is important, too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Industry observers note that LOW-IMPACT EXERCISES might be forever buzzy, but the running community is going stronger than ever. From 5Ks to marathons, lots of women are lacing up to go for a run and getting all the physical and mental health benefits that come with it. Data suggests running is great for everything from cardiovascular fitness to a healthier mindset, and it may even lower your risk of eight major diseases, making it a solid fitness habit to get into. And then there’s the fact that running makes you feel like you’ve accomplished something amazing (because you have).

As a former competitive runner who still throws down high mileage (50 to 60 miles weekly), I’ve learned the right footwear is crucial for allowing you to continue to pound the pavement, and selecting the right kind of running shoe is important, too. The best running shoes for women provide support and cushioning, with the perfect level of fit to help you forget about your footwear while you run.

While you can skimp on some fitness gear, a quality pair of running shoes is an important investment, according to Melissa Lockwood, DPM, a podiatrist at Heartland Foot and Ankle Associates in Bloomington, Illinois “I am very much in the camp of paying for a really good pair of running shoes,” she says. “It can help really minimize injury in the future.” (Still, if you’re on a tight budget or just want to save a buck, these are our favorite cheap running shoes.).

But, before taking the plunge on racking up miles, it’s key to figure out what kind of heel-to-toe drop, toe box, stability, cushioning, and heel stack is best for you. Finding the perfect running shoes involves understanding how specific design elements impact your comfort, performance, and overall experience.

There is no right or wrong, as everyone has different needs (and those needs for running shoes differ from walking shoes), but we'll go over the most vital factors to consider when shopping for running shoes.

Industry observers note that hoka does it right when it comes to a durable, high-quality shoe—specifically the Clifton 11, which was released in July 2026 in tandem with the higher-performance-oriented Clifton Pro. The Clifton family has been a crowd pleaser in the running community and amongst WH editors for a long time, and with good reason.

It has been revealed that the Clifton 11 is considered one of the brand’s most versatile running shoes, making it a good fit for everyone from beginners to seasoned pros. WH style editor Shannon Zitz says her feet never felt fatigued while she was testing this shoe, even with plantar fasciitis. “There’s technically a rocker shape built into the sole, but it's subtle enough that I barely noticed it—instead, my stride just felt smooth and natural whether I was walking or running,” she says.

According to recent reports, the Clifton 11 has an eight-millimeter heel-to-toe drop to help alleviate pressure on the plantar fascia, and the brand shaved off almost half an ounce from the weight of the model’s previous version, the Clifton 10, primarily through weight-saving revisions to the shoe’s upper. This was the primary change, with Hoka keeping the midsole that we know and love the same.

Sources indicate that these shoes offer maximum cushioning you’ll feel—the same EVA foam found in the Bondi 9 without the extra bulk. Just be aware that these don’t offer any stability innovations for flat feet, which is especially essential if you’re prone to overpronation. As for fit, the toe box does run narrow, but luckily, wide sizing is available.

Read More: Hoka Clifton 11 vs. Hoka Clifton Pro.

On has built an empire out of its highly cushioned Cloudmonster line. But its most cushioned shoe of all is the Cloudmonster 3 Hyper, an impressively bouncy sneaker that’ll make you feel like a gazelle bounding down the street.

It has been revealed that it’s generally accepted that the more cushioning a shoe has, the heavier its weight (because of all that foam packed into the midsole). But the On Cloudmonster 3 Hyper manages to deliver a highly cushioned shoe in a relatively lightweight 7.5 oz package. The result is a next-level energy return that feels like it’s propelling you forward with each step.

This sneaker has a soft, breathable upper to minimize foot sweat, along with a highly padded heel collar that lowers the risk of rubbing. I’ve worn a lot of running shoes, and that heel collar may be the thickest I’ve ever seen. There’s a nice, roomy toe box, too.

Recent findings suggest that while there’s a lot to love about the Cloudmonster 3 Hyper, it’s not perfect. This shoe’s $220 price tag puts it out of reach for many, and the tongue is on the thin side (not a deal-breaker, but some people prefer something more padded). Still, if you have the budget for it and like to feel like you’re running on actual clouds, this is a solid choice.

Read More: Best On Walking Shoes.

Industry observers note that think of a daily trainer as the chameleon of the running shoe world. This sneaker needs to be able to be durable enough for regular use, comfortable, and versatile enough to handle higher mileage along with speedier runs. The Adidas Adizero Evo SL was designed with all of that in mind, serving up a highly adaptable shoe that works for nearly everyone. That’s probably why this shoe keeps landing on the feet of runners all over the place.

Sources indicate that the Adizero Evo SL has a soft, bouncy feel underfoot and plenty of energy return thanks to Adidas’ proprietary Lightstrike Pro foam packed into the midsole. It’s also relatively lightweight, clocking in at just under 8 oz. The shoe’s peppy sensation and slight rocker shape support your stride but don’t push you forward in a way that feels unnatural.

This sneaker has an engineered mesh upper to let your feet breathe, even when you’re clocking some serious mileage. This shoe has a slightly tapered toe box, which isn’t for everyone. The outsole is also a little flat and isn’t the grippiest you’ll find, but road runners are unlikely to have an glitch. While you’re probably not choosing a running shoe based on looks alone, it doesn’t hurt that the Adizero Evo SL looks sleek.

Sources indicate that the best shoe for recovery runs is a total workhorse, delivering enough stability and cushioning to keep you comfortable as you move along at a moderate pace. The Brooks Ghost Max 3 is up for the challenge, with a wide, stable base and supportive feel to take the pressure off your joints.

This isn’t a stability shoe, per se—it won’t work to correct your stride—but it still creates a sense like you’re not going to roll an ankle or have any other gait issues as you pound the pavement. The Ghost Max 3 is a heavier shoe, although I haven’t noticed any fatigue or extra drag in it. But this sneaker holds up well to high-volume running. I wear this regularly and have never noticed any durability issues.

Recent findings suggest that the Ghost Max 3 features nitrogen-infused DNA Loft v3 foam for support and cushioning. However, it won’t give you a sinking-in feel and there is limited energy return, which could be a pro or con, depending on what you’re after. This sneaker also has a jacquard mesh upper that feels a little softer than many other running shoes out there. The Ghost Max 3 provides plenty of room, from the midfoot to the toe box, making it a good fit for people with wider feet. Just don’t plan to do any speed work in this shoe—it’s a little too heavy for that.

Read More: Brooks Ghost Max 3 Review.

Recent findings suggest that it's clear that Lululemon’s Wildfeel was designed by people who actually do trail running. It has features you want in a trail running shoe beyond just good grip.

According to recent reports, there’s a knitted sock-like upper that molds to your foot to keep out pebbles and other debris, along with a toe bumper to protect your feet over rugged terrain. I took these shoes on several runs over a rocky trail near my house, along with a few beach runs, and was impressed at how well it kept the stuff outside from getting into my shoe.

The Wildfeel has a dual-density midsole, which means that it helps give you a feeling of moving forward when you're going up hills and absorbs impact when you’re going down.

Like many other Lululemon shoes, the toe box runs a little narrow. My heel slipped around a little when I first wore these shoes, although that’s pretty common in a trail shoe, and it got better with time and more wear.

Read More: Best Trail Running Shoes.

There’s a wide range of shoes that consider themselves “stability” sneakers, but the Hoka Arahi 8 does a solid job correcting your stride with each step without being annoying. Many stability shoes are clunky and heavy, but the Arahi 8 manages to be lightweight at just 7.7 oz.

The Arahi 8 features a lot of changes from the previous version, the Arahi 7. This shoe uses special H-frame technology, featuring foam at the inner and outer foot, to deliver a more balanced support system. It’s roomy and comfortable, too. But this shoe is clearly not for everyone.

The level of stability is high, and that constant gait correction may feel like too much for some people. It also isn’t very responsive, so you’re not getting much back from your shoe with each stride other than security. (To be fair, though, that’s what people are usually after with a stability shoe.) Still, the Arahi 8 is impressively cushioned and very comfortable, whether you’re working your way through a long training session or just going out on a daily run.

In a recent development, long runs require plenty of cushioning to support you along the way. The Nike Vomero Plus, which won the award for Best Cushioned Running Shoe in the 2026 Women’s Health Fitness Awards, is here to help. This shoe delivers a fun, bouncy feel that helps propel you as you rack up the miles.

Industry observers note that the Vomero Plus has a roomy toe box and overall comfortable feel, serving up a shoe that makes long runs a little more seamless. That bounciness comes courtesy of Nike’s ZoomX foam, which is positioned along the length of the shoe. The engineered upper is crafted from yarn for a soft, breathable sensation.

Sources indicate that the Vomero Plus provides a grippy outsole, making it perfect for the pavement. But if you’re looking for a stability shoe, the Vomero Plus isn’t it. Its high heel stack and bounciness is too much for that. But if you want a highly cushioned feel as you log some serious miles, this is an excellent choice.

According to recent reports, the right race day shoe has the tough challenge of being supportive, cushiony, and lightweight, helping you to hit a PR without feeling like your footwear is holding you back. The Newly introduced Balance FuelCell SuperComp Elite v5 is designed with longer-distance racers (think: half and marathon runners) in mind, but can still be an excellent choice for 5Ks and 10Ks thanks to its lightweight (6 oz) construction and solid energy return.

Let’s get this out of the way now: At $265, this is not a cheap shoe. With that, it’s unlikely to be a good investment for the occasional racer. But if your weekends are booked with road races, it’s worth at least considering.

It has been revealed that this shoe delivers a locked-in feel, along with great traction to give you more confidence, even over wet surfaces. The roomy toe box and breathable upper also reinforce the FuelCell SuperComp Elite v5’s comfortable feel. This shoe is stable without sacrificing punchiness, helping you to feel supported as you stride. Just be aware that the midfoot and heel may feel a little too narrow for those with wider feet. But, luckily, this sneaker is available in wide widths, too.

Read More: Best Running Shoes for Plantar Fasciitis.

The lululemon Beyondfeel running shoes truly live up to their name. They’re comfortable at the heels (and everywhere), with a heel stack that provides just the right amount of cushioning. It absorbs impact while still feeling responsive, especially during long runs. Plus, the cushioning around the ankle delivers security in every step.

Recent findings suggest that the heel-to-toe drop is also a game changer—it really makes a difference for runners who heel-strike. Instead of feeling the usual jarring sensation from heel-striking, there are smooth transitions from each step. The bounce in the heel also makes it easier to maintain a steady stride without losing momentum, which is a huge benefit for runners who naturally land on their heels. The shoes guide feet to strike with the midfoot instead of the heel.

These shoes feel slightly bouncy while you run, and offer decent grip for trails and roads, making for a versatile running shoe. If you’re an overpronator, this isn’t the shoe for you—it doesn’t provide enough medial support (on the inside of the shoe). But it’s got plenty of features to make running a dream for heel strikers.

Read More: Best lululemon Shoes Ranked.

There’s a range in severity with overpronators, and what works for one won’t work for everyone. But the Asics Gel-Nimbus 28 does a solid job trying to please everyone in the overpronation camp. This shoe delivers a feel that’s not too soft or too firm, giving you the support and stability you need without feeling like you’re in a “special” shoe.

It has been revealed that this shoe is lightweight for a stability shoe at 8.5 oz, making it good for most runs that don’t involve speed work. It also delivers a solid, locked-in sensation to make you feel secure with each step. The shoe’s OrthoLite sockliner also supports that cozier feel. The Gel-Nimbus 28 feels slightly springy underfoot, which is rare for a stability shoe. (Still, the overall effect isn’t very responsive compared to non-stability shoes.).

Sources indicate that asics in general tends to run narrow and the Gel-Nimbus 28 is no exception. If your feet tend to teeter between regular and wide sizes, you may want to consider hedging your bets and trying out a larger size.

Industry observers note that the best shoe for speed work is very different from what you need for distance training or even race day. The Saucony Endorphin Azura is a lightweight (7.5 oz) shoe with a snappy feel that still manages to make you feel stable and locked in as you zip around.

The Saucony Endorphin Azura uses Pebax foam to create a responsive, bouncy feel, making you feel a little faster than usual. It also has a wide and stable base for added security during training. While it’s designed for speed, you can still comfortably wear this sneaker for longer runs and daily mileage. Just be aware that the shoe’s special SpeedRoll technology may feel slightly awkward at slower speeds.

According to recent reports, the Endorphin Azura’s outsole features XT-900 rubber for a grippy feel underfoot, making you feel comfortable pushing the pace. Saucony shoes are known for a narrower fit, and the Endorphin Azura is no exception. If you have wider feet, it may be best to look elsewhere. (It unfortunately doesn’t come in wide sizes.).

Maximum Cushioning: This type of cushion feels amazingly plush and has excellent shock absorption, which is essential for long-distance running. While they’re designed to minimize the impact on the joints, they’re not the best for speed workouts unless the shoe has a lower heel-to-toe drop and some firmness.

Sources indicate that medium: If you want to balance speed with stability, medium cushioning is ideal. Too much cushioning can cause runners with flat feet to overpronate more from the bulkiness and softness. So, this type of cushioning is best if you want a more aligned gait.

This is the difference in height between the heel and front part (known as the forefoot) of the shoe. It can impact how your foot lands on the ground when you run. Low drops (0 to 4 mm) are flatter and encourage a natural running style where you land in the middle or front of your foot. They’re great if you like to feel close to the ground, enjoy trail running, or prefer a minimalist shoe design. Medium drop (5 to 8 mm) is a versatile option that offers mid-height and cushioning—this works well for most running styles. High drop (9 to 12 mm) tends to have more height in the heel to absorb impact (this is great for heel-strikers).

According to recent reports, this is the height of the cushion under the heel. It’s measured from the outsole (the bottom of the shoe) to the insole (where your foot rests). Higher stacks offer more softness for long-distance running or for those who need less impact on the joints. Prioritizing this means sacrificing ground feel, and for some, that may feel unbalanced given the additional height.

Running shoes can provide a slew of benefits to suit your feet, but podiatrists stress the importance of getting a well-fitting shoe. “The shoe should fit your foot well and not cause any rubbing on the toes,” says Richard H. Graves, DPM, a podiatrist at Sol Foot & Ankle Centers in Long Beach, California “They should feel comfortable immediately upon putting them on and walking around.”.

Consider these areas of the shoe when checking the fit:.

It has been revealed that toe Box: This is the front part of the shoe where the toes sit. Toes spread naturally when you have extra room in the toe box, and this is especially crucial during long runs since feet can swell. But if the toe box is too big, it can lead to sliding and instability in the shoes.

Length: Since feet often swell from pounding pavement, it’s a good idea to have about a thumb’s width away from the tip of the shoe to your toe. If you’re unsure of your size, the best bet is to visit a running store to get properly fitted.

Arch Support: Those with flat feet and overpronators (when your foot lands on your outside heel and rolls inward) will want to look for shoes with enough firmness and high arch support to help keep feet aligned. Too much cushioning can create an unbalanced feeling, which can further aggravate pain. Those with neutral to high arches will have no concerns wearing shoes with neutral support. Most shoes specify which arch type they accommodate, so make sure to read their product descriptions. And, definitely don’t wear shoes with no arch support—your feet need support.

Recent findings suggest that the type of running workouts you plan to do will dictate elements like cushioning, support, and weight. More cushioning is often better with daily training and distance runs. You may also get away with a slightly heavier (but not too heavy) shoe, which usually means there’s more cushioning and stability. But shoes for speed work and race day tend to have less cushioning and a lighter weight, making it easier to move faster. For a deep-dive into the topic of running shoe selection, check out our story about how to figure out which type of running shoe you need.

Sources indicate that A stability shoe can help correct gait complications like overpronation, which is when your foot rolls inward excessively when you run or walk. Not everyone needs a stability shoe, but some level of stability is important for reducing injury risk when you’re an overpronator. There are a few ways to tell if you overpronate, per Graves: Your feet appear to be rolling inward when you stand in a relaxed position and the heels of shoes you’ve worn are tilted inward.

You should switch out your running shoes every 300 to 500 miles. An easy way to maximize your shoe lifespan is to have a few pairs that you rotate between runs. Also, if you visually see them degrading, it's time to snag a newly introduced pair.

Running shoes can be washed in cold water in the washing machine with light detergent, or spot-cleaned with a sponge. But, you should never put your shoes in the dryer—they can shrink! Instead, let them air dry in the sun.

According to recent reports, A simple at-home way to determine your arch type is the wet footprint test. You simply dip your foot in the water and step onto paper. If you see your entire foot, you have flat feet. Your foot will look like a comma if you have high arches, while a neutral arch will show slight elevation.

Industry observers note that I’ve tested dozens of pairs of running shoes to determine which make the cut for the best running shoes for women. As a personal trainer, fitness writer, and runner with years of experience testing running shoes, I put each pair to the test during two-mile runs where I evaluated key performance factors such as cushioning, stability, comfort, support, traction, and responsiveness. I also considered how well the shoes supported my stride and whether or not they helped me maintain a consistent pace. Additionally, WH fitness editors provided feedback on select shoes they love to wear during training and racing.
